Battery comparisons vary: Dave2D called it the longest seen on a 14-inch laptop, while Just Josh found a MacBook Air M3 lasted longer (Just Josh) and Laptop Mag measured 14 hours 14 minutes, behind the Surface Laptop 7 and MacBook Air M3 (Laptop Mag). Constant Geekery found multicore comfortably ahead of the M3 MacBook Air but graphics and single core behind it (Constant Geekery), and several reviewers advise checking Windows on Arm app support before buying, with gaming weak.

highlights.text: checking Windows on Arm app support

paras: Reviewers such as Engadget and Tom's Hardware like it for artists and editors who want the pull-forward hinge, an excellent keyboard and pen support. Mixed takes come mostly from price and speed: a MacBook Pro 14 gives better battery, display and performance (Matthew Moniz), and the Lenovo Legion Slim 5 14 is faster for much less (Notebookcheck). Battery results also split on the RTX 4060 64GB versions, from 11 hours 15 minutes of video at 150 nits (Notebookcheck) to about 1.5 hours of gaming (Rozetked).

Reviewers mostly see a budget 1080p 144Hz gaming laptop, one that suits students and casual players (Tally Ho Tech), with a keyboard they like and playable frame rates, including about 120 FPS in Apex Legends on the RTX 4060 16GB version (Eddie's DL). Mixed takes come from value and speed: the RTX 4050 16GB version was last in several games and judged a poor deal next to the Dell G16 7630 (Tom's Hardware), and it trails some older RTX 3060 laptops (PCMag UK). Battery life splits too, with 4 hours 43 minutes at 150 nits on the RTX 4050 16GB model (Tom's Hardware), four or five hours on the RTX 4050 8GB model (Tally Ho Tech) and 7:16 in a video loop on the RTX 4050 16GB model (PCMag UK).

Reviewers mostly praise strong 1080p and 1440p gaming for the money, though many call the screen dim. Price splits opinion: the UK price is called solid but the US price absurd, with the Lenovo Legion 5 and its OLED screen cheaper in the US (PC Gamer), while the i9 and RTX 5060 model left Binosha Tech recommending the Legion 5, ASUS TUF F16, Acer Nitro V16 or HP Victus instead (Binosha Tech). Battery depends on use: the Core i7 and RTX 5060 model lasted 71 minutes in a gaming test against 112 for the TUF Gaming A16 (PC Gamer), but reached 6 hours 10 minutes of video and browsing (PC Guide).

Reviewers praise the thin, light metal body, the bright AMOLED screen and the large trackpad, and suit it to students, travellers and everyday web users. Battery life is where takes split: on the Core 3 100U model with 8GB, Laptop Mag measured 11 hours 12 minutes in a web test, while Android Central reported four to five hours on most days and Notebookcheck saw about five hours in everyday use with the keyboard backlight on. Several reviewers call the price high for a non-touch Chromebook, and buyers who want a touchscreen are pointed to the Acer Chromebook Plus Spin 714 (PCWorld).

highlights.text: four to five hours on most days

paras: Reviewers see an office ThinkPad with a pleasant keyboard, upgradeable RAM and a matte screen, and stevenswall found it boots and opens Excel faster than a 2012 ThinkPad W530 (stevenswall). Mixed takes come from performance and battery: Notebookcheck rates it a step below the ThinkPad T14 Gen 5 (Notebookcheck) and measured 13h 40min in a Wi-Fi test on the Core Ultra 5 125U model, while Thurrott recorded about 5.5 hours of real-world use on the Core Ultra 7 155U model. Thurrott suggests most buyers pick a newer Lunar Lake, Snapdragon X or Zen 5 laptop (Thurrott), and Notebookcheck found the fan reached 46.2 dB(A) under load on its Core Ultra 5 125U unit.

Reviewers who tested the Core Ultra 9 275HX and RTX 5080 version mostly describe a desk-bound desktop replacement, praising the rigid build, the Cherry MX keyboard, three M.2 slots and Thunderbolt 5, while criticizing battery life, a weight over 7 lbs and the missing Ethernet port. Takes split on rivals: the laptop beat the Legion Pro 7i in lab game runs (Tom's Guide), but an identical Legion Pro 7i came out slightly faster (XDA Developers) and about 3 to 4% ahead and quieter (Technic-Ali), and the Legion also won on OLED, weight and built-in Ethernet (Laptop Buying Guide). Heat is also disputed, with the cooling called quiet (Notebookcheck) while the CPU hit 105C in Cinebench and the Alienware 18 Area-51, Legion Pro 7i or Razer Blade 16 were suggested instead (Mash IT).

Reviewers praise the M5 MacBook Air as a light, silent, fanless laptop with battery that lasts well past a workday and a keyboard and trackpad many rate highly, and say it suits most people. Gains over the M4 Air are small in daily use (Engadget), M4 users are told to stay put (TechRadar), and it ranks above the MacBook Neo for multitasking (Tom's Hardware). Mixed takes center on the 60Hz screen, a minor quibble on the 16GB, 1TB unit (Engadget) but dated for the price on the 10-core GPU model (Macworld), and on sustained load, where the 10-core GPU, 1TB unit throttled in a stress test (Tom's Hardware).

highlights.text: battery that lasts well past a workday

paras: Reviewers praise the aluminum build, keyboard and trackpad for students, light users and first-time Mac buyers, with battery life reported at about 7 to 8 hours of mixed use (GregsGadgets) and 13 hours 28 minutes in a streaming and browsing test (Tom's Hardware). Takes on the 8GB of RAM differ: it held up with about 20 Chrome tabs and a Lightroom export (Hardware Canucks), while 21 tabs and 12 programs pushed memory pressure to yellow (Switch and Click). Next to the M5 MacBook Air, the Neo has about half the multi-core speed and a slower SSD (Max Tech), and the Air is called the better all-round pick for anyone needing more features or able to pay more (The Guardian).

Reviewers mostly praise the aluminum build, the tandem OLED and the haptic trackpad, with the Core Ultra X7 358H version favoured for its Arc B390 graphics and the IPS versions for battery, such as 43 hours of web browsing on the Core Ultra 7 355 (Hardware Canucks). Mixed takes come from power and price: Dell caps the X7 near 27 watts, leaving it about 16% behind a Lenovo Slim 7i Ultra in Cinebench R26 multi-core (Matthew Moniz), and a cheaper M5 MacBook Air outruns the entry XPS (The Verge). The keyboard also splits opinion, with typing errors reported by Engadget and Tom's Hardware but praise from Zip Tie Tech.

Reviewers mostly praise the tandem OLED screen, slim aluminum body and webcam, and the Core Ultra X7 versions handled photo and video editing, with playable games on integrated graphics. Battery results on the Core Ultra X7 versions vary widely, from 18 hours 31 minutes in PCMark 10 Modern Office (BsianTech) to 11:53 in Modern Office (Engadget) and 10 hours 26 minutes of mixed use, behind the ASUS ExpertBook Ultra and MacBook Pro M5 (01net). The keyboard divides opinion, with TECHAERIS loving it while Engadget calls shallow travel the weak spot, and the integrated graphics trail RTX 5070 laptops (PCMag).

Reviewers who liked it point to long battery life and a quiet, cool aluminum chassis, and Notebookcheck measured 16:41 hours of web surfing at 150 nits on the Snapdragon X Plus unit. Mixed takes come from the 60Hz screen and from sibling comparisons, with the 13.8-inch model called the better buy at similar prices (Notebookcheck) and worth the extra (This Is), and the Surface Laptop 7 rated better on screen, trackpad and speakers (Bytes & Bets). The M4 MacBook Air costs more and beats all the Surfaces in many tests (The Verge), while Windows on Arm app gaps still limit photo editors and gamers.

Reviewers mostly praise the 120Hz AMOLED screen, the light aluminum body and the Galaxy phone features, and it suits Samsung phone users who want a slim Windows laptop (XDA Developers). Mixed takes come from performance and battery: the Core Ultra 5 226V model took 3 minutes 15 seconds on a DaVinci Resolve 4K render against 1 minute 35 seconds on a 13-inch M4 MacBook Air (Digit), and the MacBook Air also wins on performance and battery life (Notebookcheck), while the Core Ultra 7 256V unit lasted 15 hours 28 minutes in PCMark 10 (Trusted Reviews) against about 10 hours of browsing on the 226V model (Notebookcheck). Common complaints are shallow key travel, weaker speakers than a MacBook (Digit, Naseem Speach) and PWM flicker (Notebookcheck).

Reviewers praise the speed and battery of the Kompanio Ultra 910 models, with about 14 to 15 hours in the tests that gave a figure, and recommend it to people who live in Chrome and Google services. It beats Lenovo's Chromebook Plus 14 in some web benchmarks (PCWorld), though that Lenovo has a more accurate OLED panel (Tom's Guide) and The Verge would pick its OLED model for a high-end Chromebook (The Verge). Complaints center on the price, a jumpy trackpad on the 16GB unit (Android Police) and muddy speakers (The Verge).

Reviewers recommend it to power users who want the faster chip and can skip the touchscreen PROLED models, with Tom's Hardware measuring a 10 percent single-core Geekbench gain over last year's M5 (Tom's Hardware). Some say to wait for the expected M6 MacBook Air (Macworld), and PCMag expects that Air to make the Pro a tough sell, while also finding an RTX Spark laptop ahead in every graphics contest (PCMag). GoriMe found 16GB a little short for heavy work, with video export slower than their own M4 Max (GoriMe).

highlights.text: make the Pro a tough sell
16GB a little short for heavy work

paras: Reviewers recommend it to students and everyday users who stay in browsers and documents, praising 14 to nearly 20 hours of battery and the light aluminum build. Tom's Hardware slightly prefers it over the MacBook Neo for lighter weight and a backlit keyboard (Tom's Hardware), and Reviewed likes its touchscreen over the MacBook Neo too (Reviewed). Memory matters: Tom's Hardware found the 8GB model lags in multitasking, while Notebookcheck's 8GB unit showed graphics too weak for gaming and a chassis more fragile than older XPS 13s (Notebookcheck).

Reviewers recommend it to buyers who value repairability and a sturdier chassis and can absorb a very high price. Battery results differ by config: 15 hours 55 minutes on the Core Ultra X9 388H with 64GB (Tom's Hardware), 16 hours 48 minutes on the X7 385H (Tom's Guide), 16 hours 5 minutes on the X7 358H (Engadget) and 19 hours 18 minutes on the X7 358H (Notebookcheck), against about 10.5 hours on the X7 358H with many Chrome tabs open (The Verge). On speed, The Verge found it behind the MacBook Pro 14 M5 (The Verge), Tom's Hardware says an M5 Max MacBook Pro would beat it (Tom's Hardware), and Notebookcheck saw the CPU above 90 C under load.

Reviewers recommend it to gamers who want RTX 5080 or 5090 power and a lovely 240Hz OLED, and who accept loud fans and a high price. Against the Razer Blade 16 (2025), The Verge found the Blade's RTX 5090 led by an average of just 3.5 fps without frame generation (The Verge), and Tom's Hardware credits its 55 W CPU for stronger 1080p results than the 28W chip there (Tom's Hardware). Notebookcheck's RTX 5090 unit ran about 20 percentage points faster than the Razer Blade 16 and Zephyrus G16 (Notebookcheck), while Geeknetic found battery life weak on the RTX 5080 model, at a little over two hours at maximum brightness (Geeknetic).

Reviewers recommend it to business users who want all-day battery and full x86 app support, with 18h 13min on the Core Ultra 7 258V in PCMark 10 (TechRadar) and over 18 hours on the Core Ultra 7 268V in Techaeris's use (Techaeris), against 12 hours of web surfing on the 258V (Notebookcheck). PCMag calls the design nearly identical to the Snapdragon EliteBook Ultra G1q (PCMag), and Notebookcheck finds the Intel version better, about 150 grams lighter with a much better screen (Notebookcheck). PCMag points to the ThinkPad X1 Carbon Gen 13 Aura Edition as the work laptop to beat (PCMag), and complaints include soldered memory and, for Notebookcheck, a shallow keyboard.

Reviewers recommend it to business buyers who want power, a good keyboard and an OLED option, not light weight. Battery depends on the config: 14h 12min on the IPS Ryzen AI 9 HX PRO 375 (Notebookcheck), about 11 to nearly 13 hours on the 64GB OLED models (PCWorld, Trusted Reviews, TechRadar) and 14h 29min on the Ryzen AI 7 PRO 360 (IT Pro), with Trusted Reviews finding battery well behind the Dell Pro 14 Premium (Trusted Reviews). Notebookcheck measured it over 500 g heavier than the ThinkPad X1 Carbon Gen 13 (Notebookcheck), and Laptop Mag suggests the MSI Summit 13 AI+ Evo as a cheaper alternative while finding the keys squishy (Laptop Mag).

Reviewers praise the 240Hz OLED, cooling and raw power, and suit it to buyers who stay plugged in. Battery lasted 3 hours 20 minutes on the RTX 5090 version in the tests of Laptop Mag and Tom's Hardware, less than half the Razer Blade 16's 7 hours 21 minutes (Tom's Hardware), and Windows Central measured an 80 percent GPU drop off the charger, while the RTX 5080 unit got 8 hours 48 minutes (High Performance Laptops). Gaming rankings differ: Laptop Mag put it last among its rivals in Cyberpunk 2077 (Laptop Mag), Notebookcheck found the CPU up to 10 percent slower than the same chip in the Legion Pro 7i (Notebookcheck), and Windows Central picked the Lenovo Legion Pro 7i as its favorite 16-inch laptop (Windows Central).

highlights.text: 80 percent GPU drop off the charger

paras: Reviewers recommend it to students and everyday users who want OLED and endurance for light work. Video loops lasted over 25 hours (PCWorld) and 34 hours 48 minutes (PCMag), with Notebookcheck at 16h 56min of web surfing, though PCMag advises checking Arm app support first. The Verge would pick a Microsoft Surface Laptop or M4 MacBook Air at the regular price (The Verge), and PCWorld notes discounted Snapdragon X Elite, Ryzen AI 7 or Core Ultra 7 laptops tend to beat it (PCWorld), while weak 3D performance and glare on the glossy panel are the main complaints.

Reviewers recommend the Core Ultra 7 255H model for buyers who want strong value and speed, with YouTube loops of 12 hours 54 minutes to 17 hours 23 minutes across the two models tested by thehikaku and 16 hours 11 minutes on the 255H (これがおすすめノートパソコン). Config matters: thehikaku found the Core Ultra 7 255U model slower, with a 1920x1200 screen covering 61 percent of sRGB, one fan and no Performance mode, while the Core Ultra 5 225U unit with 512GB was called modest, with up to 8 hours of video (android.com.pl). Two reviewers measured it heavier than HP states, and the keyboard travel is shallow.

Reviewers recommend it to professionals who want a light workstation with strong CPU power and a good OLED screen. They differ on graphics and battery: TechRadar found the Radeon 8060S cannot beat the RTX 3500 in the Dell Precision 7780 (TechRadar), PCMag named the Dell Precision 5490 as its pick for weighing less and lasting longer (PCMag), and StorageReview found local AI work slower than an older ThinkPad P15 Gen 2 with an RTX A5000 (StorageReview). Battery varied by config, from 6h 48min of video on the OLED unit (PCMag) to 15h 27min on the Ryzen AI MAX PRO 390 IPS model (High Performance Laptops).

Reviewers recommend it to people who work on the go and type a lot, as a light, cheaper alternative to the X1 Carbon Gen 14 (thehikaku.net). That reviewer found the X1 Carbon Gen 14 faster, with a haptic touchpad and about 100 g less weight, and the older X1 Carbon Gen 13 cheaper with longer battery life (thehikaku.net); slide-style.com found the HP EliteBook X G2i 14 with the same chip about 10 percent higher in Cinebench R23 multi-core (slide-style.com). Under load, tabletpcnavi.com measured the CPU package at 96 degrees and fan noise of 44.5 dB (tabletpcnavi.com), while slide-style.com said the fan was not noticeable.

Reviewers say it suits students and buyers who want speed and endurance with Arm-native apps, with battery results including 19 hours 42 minutes in a PCMark 10 video loop (Trusted Reviews) and 28 hours 48 minutes of local video (PCMag), against about 14 hours of real use in Performance mode (Windows Central). PCWorld compared it with the ThinkPad T14s Gen 6 and the MSI Prestige Flip 14 AI+ and found Snapdragon gives no clear battery edge (PCWorld), and also reported YouTube hitching and several keyboard lockups. Price draws criticism, since both PCMag and Trusted Reviews point to the Asus Zenbook A14 with the same or almost identical specs for less money (PCMag, Trusted Reviews).

Reviewers recommend it to people who want a light laptop with long runtimes, with 19h 36min of web surfing (Notebookcheck) and over 20 hours of video (NETZWELT), against 16h 03min of Full HD video (CHIP). NETZWELT weighed it at 1,220 grams, against 2.15 kilograms for a 16-inch MacBook Pro (NETZWELT), and lists the MacBook Pro with M4 and the ThinkPad X9-14 Gen 1 as alternatives (NETZWELT). Notebookcheck noted slight thermal throttling, a slightly bendy case and weaker graphics than the RTX 3050 of its predecessor (Notebookcheck), and NETZWELT and CHIP both miss a fingerprint sensor.

highlights.text: a light laptop with long runtimes

paras: Reviewers praise an excellent keyboard and haptic touchpad, and on the Snapdragon X2 Plus version they measured 18h 53min of web surfing (Notebookcheck) and 13 hours 51 minutes of intensive web use (CHIP). Windows Central's Intel Core Ultra X7 368H business unit lasted about 8 hours, which it calls only okay and well short of the Qualcomm-powered Surface Laptop 7 (Windows Central). Notebookcheck argues private buyers would benefit from the Intel model's Arc B390 graphics but notes Microsoft sells them only the Snapdragon version (Notebookcheck), while Windows Central says standard consumers should wait for the Snapdragon models.

Reviewers say it suits developers and power users running local AI models, with The Verge calling it hard to recommend for everyone else. Against Apple, Tom's Hardware found multi-core Geekbench short of the MacBook Pro M5 Max (Tom's Hardware) and The Verge found a 4K Premiere export about a minute behind the top MacBook Pro (The Verge), while StorageReview found Cinebench 2026 multi-core ahead of the Razer Blade 16 though the RTX 5090 Blade made tokens 2.3x faster on models fitting 24GB (StorageReview). Results vary by unit: The Verge found local AI felt like a beta on its 128GB unit, Tom's Hardware measured 10 hours 43 minutes of battery on the 32GB unit, and StorageReview said one unit lost power three times under one heavy all-core load.

highlights.text: hard to recommend for everyone else

paras: Reviewers suit it to desktop replacement buyers who want top gaming speed and an excellent mini-LED screen and have the budget. WIRED found it about 10 percent faster in Cyberpunk 2077 and 18 percent faster in Time Spy than the Razer Blade 16 with the same GPU (WIRED), while IGN found the Razer Blade 16 quieter and easier to carry (IGN), XDA Developers found CPU and synthetic scores only a touch faster than the 16-inch Legion Pro 7i (XDA Developers), and High Performance Laptops notes the MSI Raider A18 HX offers similar baseline performance for less (High Performance Laptops). Short battery life and loud fans come up in most reviews, and the haptic touchpad draws criticism from Notebookcheck, WIRED, PC Guide and XDA Developers.

highlights.text: Short battery life and loud fans

paras: Reviewers praise the battery, with 12 hours 46 minutes of web use in two tests (Tom's Hardware, Tom's Guide) and 11 hours 41 minutes (Notebookcheck) on the Core Ultra 9 and RTX 5090 versions, along with the vivid OLED. Tom's Hardware found multi-threaded work slower than the MSI Raider 16 Max HX and Red Dead Redemption 2 at 94fps against 121fps for last year's model (Tom's Hardware), while Notebookcheck found games 5 to 20 percent faster than the AMD model but the CPU 10 to 15 percent slower than the Ryzen AI 9 HX 370 (Notebookcheck). Tom's Guide says the Asus ROG Zephyrus Duo has the same specs but performs worse (Tom's Guide), and Notebookcheck calls the price rise hard to justify.

Reviewers suit it to home gamers near AC power who want top mobile GPU performance. Tom's Hardware found it edging out the MSI Titan 18 HX AI in every game test (Tom's Hardware), Tom's Guide called it the fastest 4K gaming laptop in its testing while trading blows with the Alienware Area-51 (Tom's Guide), and Engadget prefers the Blade 16 for daily carrying (Engadget). Battery is the shared complaint, with PCWorld calling battery life abysmal (PCWorld) and Windows Central measuring 1 hour 25 minutes of gaming on battery (Windows Central), and Windows Central recommends the RTX 5070 Ti or at most the RTX 5080 over the RTX 5090 for desktop replacement.

Reviewers praise the AMOLED screen and battery, with looped video lasting 19h 41min on the Core Ultra 5 226V (Notebookcheck), 20 hours 3 minutes on the Core Ultra 7 256V (TechRadar), 18 hours 43 minutes on the 258V (WIRED) and nearly 23.5 hours on the 258V (PCWorld), against about 13 hours of average use from a battery report on the Core Ultra 5 228V (Windows Central). The shallow keyboard is the most repeated complaint, and WIRED, the least positive review, also reported frequent bugs. On comparisons, PCWorld says the Dell Inspiron 16 Plus has better raw CPU speed but this laptop lasts longer (PCWorld), Notebookcheck names the HP Envy x360 as a better keyboard option (Notebookcheck), and PCWorld finds the trackpad less premium than the haptic one on the Surface Laptop 7 (PCWorld).

highlights.text: shallow keyboard is the most repeated complaint

paras: Reviewers praise the AMOLED display and sturdy metal build, with TechRadar, which used it for work and creative apps, advising against it for gamers or tight budgets (TechRadar). Battery depends on the test, from 28 hours 32 minutes of local video (PCMag) and almost 17 hours of web use (Notebookcheck) to 13 hours 39 minutes in a video test (TechRadar), while The Verge saw uneven results of 7 to over 10 hours. On the RTX 5070 model, Notebookcheck says the MacBook Pro 16 M4 Pro is clearly faster with a brighter screen (Notebookcheck), TechRadar says the MacBook Pro beats its battery by about five hours (TechRadar), and The Verge found the MacBook Pro 14 M5 handily wins the 4K video export (The Verge).

highlights.text: AMOLED display and sturdy metal build

paras: Reviewers praise the Crave as a comfortable, low-profile fairway driver that flips up from a hyzer, rides straight and goes farther than its 6.5 speed suggests, especially for beginners, slower arms and woods shots. Takes split on stability: Flippy James Disc Golf finds the Neutron the most overstable of its Neutron, Fission and Proton Craves and the Proton the most understable, while Cheating Lefty Disc Golf finds the Plasma the most overstable and the Fission in between. Part Time Disc Golf thinks weight may explain the flip more than plastic, with the lighter Craves flipping more. Pete Collins Disc Golf finds the Crave and Axiom Bokeh almost neck and neck, with the Bokeh slightly farther, and Nick Carroll Disc Golf finds the Plasma Crave more stable than the Innova Cheetah and a touch more stable than the Discraft Cicada.

highlights.text: comfortable, low-profile fairway driver that flips up from a hyzer
goes farther than its 6.5 speed suggests

paras: Reviewers praise it as a slower, more controllable alternative to the Innova Destroyer that gives average and intermediate arms real distance. Takes split on plastic: IceBerg TV finds Pro the most flippy and Star by far the most stable, while Inside the Circle DG found DX and Pro turned over easily as arm strength grew and Champion hard to turn over. Bodanza Disc Golf finds the I-Blend flippier and glidier than a stock Star Wraith, and Part Time Disc Golf finds the Halo version holds an anhyzer longer than Star. Part Time Disc Golf also notes the Innova Racer outdrove the Halo Wraith by a good 80, maybe 90 ft, at about the same strength.

highlights.text: slower, more controllable alternative to the Innova Destroyer
DX and Pro turned over easily as arm strength grew
flippier and glidier than a stock Star Wraith

paras: Reviewers praise it as a reliable overstable approach disc that handles forehand torque and holds a line. Flippy James Disc Golf, Bradley Martin and Chains on Tap all find it flies very close to the Discraft Zone, so feel in the hand and the plastic decide between them. Plastic matters: Beaver Branch Disc Golf Adventures finds the Moonshine most stable and the VIP and Origio least stable, while No Budget Disc Golf Videos finds a newer BT Medium a lot more stable than an older, beat-up disc. Disc Golf Puttheads finds even short putts dump left quickly, so it is poor for turbo putting.

highlights.text: flies very close to the Discraft Zone
even short putts dump left quickly

paras: Reviewers praise how the Berg holds a hyzer, flat or anhyzer line and then drops with little skip or run, which makes it a reliable approach and short forehand disc. Takes split on putting and feel, since some find it a weak putter with an odd rim, while others like the grip and thumb track. Plastic differences are small: JustDisc finds K1 Soft almost identical to K1 and K3 a touch more overstable, while Disc Golf Examiner finds K1 Soft slightly more stable than K1 and K3 the most understable. Disc Golf Nerd finds the Westside Harp faster, longer carrying and with more fade, and Daddy Delp Disc Golf finds the Berg more sensitive to off-axis torque on forehand than the Westside Harp.

highlights.text: holds a hyzer, flat or anhyzer line and then drops with little skip or run
others like the grip and thumb track
some find it a weak putter with an odd rim

paras: Reviewers praise it as a comfortable, straight mid for beginners and for tight woods and gap shots, and several say it shows angle and form errors right away. Takes split on stability by plastic: Cheating Lefty Disc Golf finds the GStar the most understable, the Champion very straight and the Halo the most overstable at the finish, while Kona Montgomery finds a new Star starts very straight and beats in to understable. Some reviewers say it turns over on forehand throws and is not torque resistant, and Magnus Hedegaard finds it too straight when a shot needs fade. On comparisons, Know Your Discs finds less fade than an Innova Roc, and IceBerg TV finds less flip than the MVP Detour.

highlights.text: comfortable, straight mid for beginners and for tight woods and gap shots
turns over on forehand throws and is not torque resistant
Kona Montgomery finds a new Star starts very straight and beats in to understable

paras: Reviewers who loved it praise a straight, torque resistant mid with a shallow rim that feels comfortable, and several call the grip a highlight. Two reviewers find it more stable than expected, and one points beginners to a less stable disc. Plastic differences split opinion: Cheating Lefty Disc Golf calls Neutron one of the more understable versions, Eclipse harsher at the finish and Total Eclipse the most overstable, while Peachy Disc Golf and Discsmith Disc Golf find most plastics fly very alike, apart from a Proton Soft with extra late fade for Discsmith Disc Golf; Luce Disc Golf finds a lighter Fission more stable than a max weight Eclipse. On comparisons, 900 Rated finds it nearly identical to the Discraft Buzzz, maybe a touch more stable, and not a replacement, while Matt Hester Disc Golf calls it the most similar disc to a Discraft Buzzz seen so far.

highlights.text: a straight, torque resistant mid with a shallow rim that feels comfortable
Two reviewers find it more stable than expected
Luce Disc Golf finds a lighter Fission more stable than a max weight Eclipse

paras: Reviewers praise the Destroyer as a dependable fade driver, with some calling the Star one stable enough to throw hard without flipping and good for hyzer and forehand shots. Takes split on stability, since the same mold flies very differently by plastic, weight and wear. Cheating Lefty Disc Golf finds Halo and heavy Star very overstable, the 143 g Star understable and DX neutral, while Rippin Discs finds a new Star pretty overstable and expects a very beaten Pro to flip up on a hyzer. Myles of Discs finds the Destroyers dump at the end of the flight and swaps them for Emperors, calling the Destroyer molds more dependable than the Innova Wraith.

highlights.text: flies very differently by plastic, weight and wear
dump at the end of the flight

paras: Reviewers praise a straight, predictable mid-range that holds its line under torque and suits players of all skill levels and arm speeds. Takes split on plastic: Cheating Lefty Disc Golf calls Z Flex the straightest premium plastic out of the box and says Crystal, Glow Flex, Titanium and Big Z fly more overstable, while Ace Run Productions found the slick ESP gave less glide than other Buzzz plastics. Bodanza Disc Golf finds it less glidy than the Innova Mako3 and weaker on anhyzer lines, and Peachy Disc Golf finds it a little more overstable and less glidy than the Axiom Hex.

highlights.text: suits players of all skill levels and arm speeds
the slick ESP gave less glide than other Buzzz plastics

paras: Reviewers praise the Axiom Envy as a long-gliding, line-holding throwing putter that works for drives, approaches and some putting. Takes split on stability: Electron is the slightly understable, quick-to-break-in plastic, while Proton, Plasma and Eclipse hold straighter and fade more, and some reviewers find it a little stable for putting. Inside the Circle finds the Envy not near as overstable as the Discraft Zone, while Calculated Disc Golf places the Eagle McMahon run between the Discraft Zone and a normal stable Envy. Part Time Disc Golf finds the Axiom Tempo more stable and suggests it for flat sidearm throws, since the Envy can turn over.

highlights.text: Electron is the slightly understable, quick-to-break-in plastic
some reviewers find it a little stable for putting

paras: Reviewers praise it as a dependable overstable approach and utility putter for forehand flex lines, headwind putts and spike hyzers. Takes differ by plastic: Z is the most overstable but can feel slick and skip, the Jawbreaker is less stable and turns over once beaten in, and a beaten-in ESP can turn over too. Bodanza Disc Golf finds the swirly soft Zone flies like the Innova Pig, while Cheating Lefty Disc Golf says it fills the overstable slot the Westside Harp held before. Disc Golf Puttheads finds higher glide than the Innova Aviar3 and a harder fade than similar overstable putters.

highlights.text: dependable overstable approach and utility putter
the Jawbreaker is less stable and turns over once beaten in

paras: Reviewers praise the Pure as a straight, shallow-rimmed putter that holds the line it is thrown on, for both putting and throwing. Takes split on how stable it is: Beaver Branch Disc Golf Adventures finds it straight and slightly understable, Cheating Lefty Disc Golf calls it very neutral with little fade, and Chain Raider Disc Golf finds it turns over in a headwind. Plastics differ: Beaver Branch Disc Golf Adventures finds Zero Medium straightens out more easily than Opto, while Disc Golf Nerd finds Eco Zero straight to understable and Opto more neutral. Kyle Eberdt - Disc Golf switches from the Discraft Luna to the Pure for putting, and ICrank Disc Golf throws an Opto Pure about 265 feet against about 244 for the Axiom Envy on flat shots.

highlights.text: straight, shallow-rimmed putter that holds the line it is thrown on
Chain Raider Disc Golf finds it turns over in a headwind
Cheating Lefty Disc Golf calls it very neutral with little fade

paras: Reviewers praise the Trail for easy distance, a comfortable rim and a flight that stays near straight with a slight turn and slight fade. Takes split on stability by plastic: TK Disc Golf calls the Fission version less stable than the Neutron, with more high-speed turn and extra glide, while TBH Disc Golf finds the Proton more stable than the Neutron in a headwind. Bodanza Disc Golf finds only the Innova Gorgon more understable than the Trail, and Cheating Lefty Disc Golf finds the Trail the straightest and slightly most overstable of the three against the Innova Gorgon and the Axiom Insanity. Wind and height can change the flight, as one reviewer saw the Proton turned over in a tailwind when thrown with height, and another would not pull the Fission out in a headwind.

Reviewers praise the Wave as a distance driver for slower or moderate arms that flips up from a hyzer and finishes with a small fade, and some like the hand feel and glide. Opinions split on stability: two find it flips over hard with power and hyzers out when powered down, while another finds it stabled up and not very flippy. Plastic matters: Cheating Lefty Disc Golf finds the Proton the most overstable and the Fission the one with the most turn, and IceBerg TV finds Eclipse far more stable than Proton or Neutron. Gladiator Disc Golf finds the Wave more understable than the Innova Wraith or Dynamic Discs Trespass, while Shea Stevens says the Fission flew almost identical lines to a pre-flight MVP Photon.

highlights.text: flips up from a hyzer and finishes with a small fade
flips over hard with power and hyzers out when powered down

paras: Reviewers praise the glide and the friendly feel for slower arms, with several finding it goes a long way once thrown with some snap. Takes split on stability by plastic and run: Disc Respect Disc Golf calls the Opto a lot more understable and flippier than the Gold Ice, while Flying Fajita Disc Golf found one Opto Ice Splash run a little more overstable than expected. DiscGolf Justice finds it flippier and a little less stable than the Discmania Essence and picks the Essence for the bag, and Brook Arnold finds the Axiom Crave a little more stable and more repeatable, though the River sometimes goes as far.

highlights.text: praise the glide and the friendly feel for slower arms
flippier and a little less stable than the Discmania Essence
the River sometimes goes as far

paras: Reviewers praise it as a wind-resistant fairway driver for players wanting the Innova TeeBird hand feel with a sturdier finish. Takes split on how overstable it is: Disc Golf Nerd finds the Champion Ricky Wysocki edition much more overstable than expected, while Robert Eich finds the Tour Series run straighter and less stable than the Innova TeeBird or Innova Eagle. Plastic matters too: IceBerg TV finds an older Metal Flake Champion very stable, and Robert Eich finds Halo and Champion hold a straight line while Star and Color Glow flip over a little. Hucking Aces finds almost no glide, and GoHamDiscGolf gets about 40 feet more than the Innova TeeBird.

highlights.text: praise it as a wind-resistant fairway driver
gets about 40 feet more than the Innova TeeBird

paras: Reviewers praise it as a point and shoot, understable mid that flips up from a hyzer and holds a line, with several naming low arm speed players and the woods as its best fit. Takes split on how flippy it is: Henry Disc Golf finds it burns over quickly when thrown hard, Macktown Disc Golf found it touchy at high speed and flipped one all the way over, while Daddy Delp Disc Golf finds it much less flippy than the MVP Uplink and more controllable than expected. Zach Turpin Disc Golf says it flies like a beat up Axiom Hex out of the box, and Flippy James Disc Golf finds it turns more than the Hex but comes back instead of holding the turn. Andrew calls it the regular person's Axiom Hex, and Cheating Lefty Disc Golf sees Discmania Origin as the closest disc and Discraft Meteor as a bit flippier with a little less fade.

highlights.text: point and shoot, understable mid that flips up from a hyzer and holds a line
burns over quickly when thrown hard
much less flippy than the MVP Uplink and more controllable than expected

paras: Reviewers praise a straight, glidey putter that holds hyzer and anhyzer lines and works for putting, approaches and throwing from the tee. Takes split on plastic: Disc Golf Jedi finds the beat-in Electron Firm flattest and straightest, while the Neutron, Cosmic Neutron and Proton fly more overstable, and Jake from Disc Golf finds the premium plastics a bit more overstable than the Electron. TK Disc Golf finds the Pilot goes dead straight thrown flat where the Axiom Proxy needs a hyzer flip, while RayzorJay DG finds it glides more than the Axiom Proxy or Axiom Envy. Disc Golf Nerd finds the flight quite similar to a soft Axiom Envy, but expects a new max weight Axiom Envy to be more stable.

highlights.text: a straight, glidey putter that holds hyzer and anhyzer lines
glides more than the Axiom Proxy or Axiom Envy

paras: Reviewers praise it as a forgiving, straight-flying fairway driver that suits average arms and learners, with a fade that shows up as it slows down. Takes split on plastic: ChasinChains finds the DX very understable and flippy while the Champion is straight and stable, and Myles of Discs finds I-blend close to Star but slightly flippier. Cole Bordis finds the TeeBird holds an anhyzer turn line longer than the Discraft Athena but calls newer Star and Champion plastic flimsy. Myles of Discs says the Innova TeeBird3 feels more controllable and more trustworthy in wind.

highlights.text: finds the DX very understable and flippy
calls newer Star and Champion plastic flimsy

paras: Reviewers praise it as a control fairway driver that holds its line, then finishes left, useful in headwinds and for hyzer or flex shots. Takes split on how stable it is: some copies fade hard and short, while others turn a little when light or beat in. Chris Goodrich finds the Fission flippier than the Neutron, which fades harder and sooner, and calls the Fission very comparable to the Dynamic Discs Getaway. Bodanza Disc Golf finds a Proton flat and flippy, closer to a Discmania PD than its listed numbers, and suggests rerating it nearer 9/5/0/2.

highlights.text: praise it as a control fairway driver that holds its line, then finishes left
some copies fade hard and short

paras: Reviewers praise how it holds hard hyzers, handles torque on forehands and fades out late and predictably. Opinions split on plastics: Part Time Disc Golf finds the 147 g Fission goes straighter and further than the 178 g Eclipse but is affected more by wind, while Jake from Disc Golf finds the flight pretty much identical across plastics, with only the feel differing. Jake from Disc Golf and IceBerg TV both liken it to the Discraft Buzzz, and Sam Estes Disc Golf finds it holds up to a forehand better than the Discraft Buzzz without being super overstable. Three reviewers find little turn when new, so it is hard to turn over.

highlights.text: Three reviewers find little turn when new
it is hard to turn over

paras: Reviewers mostly praise easy distance from hyzer flips and S curves, with a flat top that feels comfortable on backhand and forehand. Takes split on stability: Disc Golf Deals USA finds Eclipse and new Neutron copies overstable while used Proton and Fission copies flip up and push straight, and Palace City Disc Golf calls the Proton and Cosmic Neutron difference night and day. Disc Golf Jedi says the glow copy flies a bit like an MVP Tesla, and Greybeard Disc Golf sees the Eclipse as a slower arm alternative to an Innova Firebird.

Reviewers praise a straight, point and shoot flight that holds the release angle, with a shallow rim that feels comfortable. Most compare it with the Axiom Envy: Nate Turner finds it dead straight but less stable, and Pop Top Disc Golf sees it flip up more than expected, with the Axiom Envy winning the scoring. Plastics differ too, as Flying Fajita Disc Golf finds the premium copies fly almost the same, while Sgambati Disc Golf finds base plastic copies turn over pretty fast. Chris Goodrich calls the Plasma copy a very neutral flyer that follows the release angle.

Reviewers praise a dependable, torque resistant overstable mid that holds its line on forehands and flex shots before a strong finish. Takes split on plastic: Cheating Lefty Disc Golf finds the Neutron the most overstable and the Fission the straightest, while Flippy James Disc Golf ranks Prism Proton as the most stable and Fission as the least. On the MVP Deflector, Disc Golf Examiner calls the Pyro less dumpy and glidier, and Daddy Disc Golf says it is not as stable. Air It Out Disc Reviews finds it flies like it has one or two glide and would not go past about 317 feet.

highlights.text: like it has one or two glide

paras: Reviewers like the glide, the rounded rim and the straight, soft landing on approaches, and many putt or throw it with confidence. Takes split on stability, with plastic and run doing most of the work: Cheating Lefty Disc Golf finds base plastics season quickly while premium plastics stay straight longer, and SHANK SQUAD finds most runs straight and inconsistent. Apollo Disc Golf sees the Axiom Pixel as loftier and more stable on putts, and IceBerg TV keeps the Axiom Proxy as the main throwing putter while recommending the Luna.

Reviewers praise a neutral, straight flight with lots of glide that holds hyzer, flat and anhyzer lines, and rate it as both a putting and a throwing putter. The bead is the main split: Ben Propes says the choice between this disc and the Dynamic Discs Warden comes down to whether a player likes a bead, and CDubbs Disc Golf suggests a Latitude 64 Pure for a shallower, beadless option. Plastic and age matter too, as Mikey DG finds a new copy more overstable and a beat in copy stable to understable. Beaver Branch Disc Golf Adventures says it held its line at full power where a Dynamic Discs Deputy or Latitude 64 Keystone would flip.

highlights.text: neutral, straight flight with lots of glide
whether a player likes a bead

paras: Reviewers call it a neutral, straight, beginner friendly putter that holds light hyzer and anhyzer lines. Takes split on use: Nick Carroll Disc Golf loves it as a training and short range putter, while JoeMamaGames finds it too stable for upshots and too fast on long putts, and says an Innova AviarX3 fills its roles better. Brook Arnold sticks with the Discmania P2 for a higher shoulder and stronger finish, and Disc Golf Puttheads (Rodney Lane) skips it as the main putter because the rim is a little too deep.

highlights.text: the rim is a little too deep

paras: Reviewers praise a reliable, aggressive fade that makes it the go-to utility disc for forehands, flex shots and wind. Takes split on how overstable it is by plastic and run: Steven Kitchens Disc Golf finds Star less overstable than Champion, and ChasinChains finds a light Star copy flippy while a Sexton Champion Glow copy flies straight with a predictable fade. Disc Golf Teacher places it less glidy and more overstable than the Discraft Raptor but not as overstable as the Discmania Splice, and Disc Golf Nerd finds a rim slightly enlarged compared with an Innova Eagle, with more stability.

highlights.text: finds a light Star copy flippy

paras: Reviewers praise a straight, forgiving flight for beginners and slower arms, with hyzer flips, turnovers and a comfortable rim. Takes split on stability by plastic: Bodanza Disc Golf finds a Star copy more overstable than its numbers, unlike the very flippy DX copies many players start with, and Titan Disc Golf says beat-in copies hyzer flip and drift right while new ones finish straighter. Nick Carroll Disc Golf calls the Innova Leopard3 slightly more stable and less glidey, and says the Innova Hawkeye and Innova TL fade harder and need more turn for a little extra distance.

Reviewers recommend it as easy distance for slower and medium arms, with hyzer flips, S curves and turnovers. Takes split on how understable it really is: Disc Golf Deals USA finds Star, Halo and Duo copies far straighter than the numbers, while Six Sided Discs finds the order of plastics flips with arm speed. Disc Golf Over 40 found it slightly shorter than the MVP Trail but the most accurate, and Nick Arnette picked it over the Innova Gorgon at a low arm speed, while IceBerg TV picked the Innova Gorgon over it.

highlights.text: easy distance for slower and medium arms

paras: Reviewers like a low-glide, overstable approach disc with a thumb track and tacky plastic that drops and sticks. Takes split on stability: IceBerg TV finds very little glide and more stability than expected, while Flippy James Disc Golf finds it less stable than another brand's approach disc and would give it a two fade instead of a three. Owen Pautlitz finds it forgiving where the Discraft Zone punishes accidental hyzer releases, and Daddy Delp Disc Golf finds forehands less stable and prone to wobble compared with a Discraft Zone or Westside Harp.

highlights.text: less stable than another brand's approach disc

paras: Suits beginners and slower arms wanting a point-and-shoot midrange, with reviewers praising its glide, grippy plastics and easy hyzer flips and turnover lines. Plastic changes the flight: Six Sided Discs placed a stiff Opto Ice Orbit copy and a flexible Frost copy nowhere near each other on a stability graph, and Beaver Branch Disc Golf Adventures found Opto domier and glidier than Retro, with Opto X a little more stable. Power is the limit, as DiscGolf Justice warns that torque makes it flip and turn over on forehands. Apollo Disc Golf found the profile of an Innova Roc3 style mid in an understable version, and Cole Bordis liked a soft hyzer flip to straight that a Discraft Buzzz cannot give without a flex line.

highlights.text: easy hyzer flips and turnover lines
torque makes it flip and turn over on forehands
nowhere near each other on a stability graph

paras: Suits amateur and intermediate arms chasing distance, with reviewers praising its glide, late turn and flip-up flights. Plastic splits takes: ChasinChains found a Champion copy went farthest every round while Halo copies turned and died into a headwind, and Disc Golf Nerd liked GStar for being soft and grippy in the cold. Headwinds are the weak spot, as Know Your Discs avoids them because it turns way too much. Brook Arnold swapped it in for the Axiom Mayhem to learn its angles.

highlights.text: glide, late turn and flip-up flights
turned and died into a headwind

paras: Suits players who want a dependable midrange that holds hyzer and anhyzer lines and finishes with a reliable fade, including in wind. Plastic matters: Cheating Lefty Disc Golf finds DX straighter and quick to season with Halo the most torque resistant, while Sandy Bear Disc Golf saw a Star copy fly a lot more overstable than a gummy Champion one. Feel and forehands are the weak spots, as the large bead and rim do not click for some reviewers and powered forehands get squirrely. Apollo Disc Golf calls the Innova RocX3 a more overstable version with a stronger finish.

highlights.text: large bead and rim do not click

paras: Suits forehand throwers and anyone wanting an overstable fairway for headwinds and flex shots, with reviewers praising the small rim, flat top and strong fade. Takes split on stability: Disc Golf Down Under calls it exactly the mini Innova Firebird, giving about 10 meters less distance, while Brook Arnold found a Neutron copy not stable enough for the slot and Hot Beef Disc Golf found it closer to a fast overstable midrange. Plastic matters, as Disc Golf Down Under says an older Neutron copy is nowhere near as stable as a newer Proton one, and Shea Stevens found an Eclipse copy too stable for long panning anhyzers.

highlights.text: small rim, flat top and strong fade
not stable enough for the slot

paras: Suits players who want a neutral putter that goes where it is thrown for putting, approach and tee shots, with reviewers praising its grip and straight flights that hold hyzer and anhyzer lines. Plastic matters: Daddy Delp Disc Golf found K3 very neutral and K1 a little more stable. The catch is that it flips up or turns over when thrown hard, and Macktown Disc Golf found it too flippy for a hard hyzer into gusts. Ryan Anderson DG preferred the slower, more forgiving flight of the Kastaplast Tuff.

highlights.text: a neutral putter that goes where it is thrown
straight flights that hold hyzer and anhyzer lines
flips up or turns over when thrown hard

paras: Suits players wanting a dependable control driver for wind and forehands, with reviewers praising its torque resistance, flat top and reliable fade. Plastic and run split takes: IceBerg TV found Electron the most understable, Proton very overstable and Plasma flattest with less glide, and Jake from Disc Golf warns that parting line height varies a lot between copies. Brook Arnold found the deep, domey rim not for them and likened it to a speed eight Innova TeeBird, while Daddy Delp Disc Golf found it straighter than the MVP Terra and Matt White Disc Golf found it glidier than the MVP Terra.

highlights.text: torque resistance, flat top and reliable fade
parting line height varies a lot between copies

paras: Suits beginners and intermediate arms wanting easy distance and predictable lines, with reviewers praising how it stays wherever it is put and flies the same backhand and forehand. Plastic splits takes: Cheating Lefty Disc Golf ranks Star the most understable, Champion neutral and GStar and Halo the wind fighters, while Big Guy Little Disc finds Halo and Champion too overstable for a slow arm. Caleb Minerd found a DX copy ridiculously understable for anyone with power, and Brook Arnold calls a Halo copy very stable for this mold. Disc Golf Over 40 felt it was a little more trustworthy than the Innova Mamba.

highlights.text: too overstable for a slow arm
ridiculously understable for anyone with power

paras: Suits moderate arm speeds that want easy S-curves, hyzer flips and roller shots, with reviewers praising the way it flips up and finishes. Plastic changes the flight: Disc Golf Deals USA found GStar and Star flying with the full rated turn, Champion, Halo and a Moondust run flying straighter, and Pro the flippiest. Wind and big arms are the limits, as GoHamDiscGolf says it is not a good wind disc and Disc Golf 101 says an arm near 400 feet flips it over. ChasinChains found a Halo copy less understable than the Innova Roadrunner, which flips up more.

highlights.text: the way it flips up and finishes

paras: Suits players who want a straight, controllable midrange that changes with wear, with reviewers praising its glide, consistency and the way it holds whatever line it is thrown on. Takes split on plastic and feel: DX beats in faster while KC Pro seasons slowly, and several reviewers dislike the dome and bead. One reviewer finds KC Pro slippery in the cold, and another saw it shatter on a tree. TBH Disc Golf and Disc Golf Underground both preferred the Discraft Buzzz, while Green Splatter (Lucas Miller) suggests the Innova Roc3 in premium plastic as an alternative.

highlights.text: holds whatever line it is thrown on

paras: Suits players who want one putter for putting, upshots and short drives, with reviewers praising its straight, glidey flight and low profile feel. Plastic splits takes: TK Disc Golf found Proton flips up and flies dead straight while Electron flips faster and turns more as it beats in, and Level 2 Disc Golf says Firm Electron held its stability after many tee shots. Matt White Disc Golf preferred the extra stability of the Axiom Envy, while Daddy Delp Disc Golf found a Fission copy flew almost like slightly stable Envies. Disc Golf Deals USA lost a putter match because it lacked stability on holes that cut back.

paras: Reviewers praise the shallow, low profile feel and a straight, repeatable flight that holds anhyzer lines and finishes with a fade, with gummy Proton Soft copies often called grippy. Takes split on stability: Ozark Mountain Discs finds an Eclipse copy really stable and close to a Discraft Zone in the bag, while Luke Jenkins Disc Golf finds a Particle Glow copy forgiving and closer to its flight numbers. Chris Zagone calls it an overstable, torque resistant approach disc that excels on sidearm approach shots, but Isaac Montez - Disc Golf finds it flies too straight on forehands with off axis releases. Jose Sanchez prefers the Axiom Balance for a harder finish at the end of the flight.

highlights.text: flies too straight on forehands with off axis releases

paras: Reviewers praise a straight, glidey flight that is easy to control for hyzer flips, tunnel shots and point and shoot lines, with plastic deciding the stability: S-Line flips up and finishes straight, while C-Line holds hyzers and fades harder. Takes split on the newer C-Line runs: Victor Folcke finds the new Swedish made C-Line stable to overstable and maybe more stable than a Latitude 64 Explorer, while Daddy Delp Disc Golf finds it more stable than expected and shorter than an Axiom Crave. Apollo Disc Golf finds the FD goes a little farther than the Axiom Crave on extra glide, and BrunoDDiscGolf gets about 30 feet more than an Innova TeeBird3. DiscGolf Justice does not trust the S-Line on forehand and finds it turns too much on flat throws.

highlights.text: goes a little farther than the Axiom Crave
turns too much on flat throws

paras: Reviewers praise a straight, reliable flight that finishes with a predictable fade and holds up in wind, used for putting, approaches and hyzer drives. Takes split on the newer Discmania made run: Foundation Disc Golf finds the stability and feel match the original, while Disc Golf Coolness finds the prototype even more overstable, dumping left fast on flat throws. Brook Arnold calls it basically the same as the Discmania P2x with a different hand feel, and Ryan Anderson DG finds the Discraft Roach flies straighter. The deep rim is the usual complaint, with Armory Disc Golf calling it uncomfortable in a power grip.

highlights.text: dumping left fast on flat throws

paras: Reviewers praise controllable, straight distance for players without a big arm, with hyzer flips that ride flat and far. Plastic changes the disc: ChasinChains finds a Halo Star copy shockingly overstable and a Pro copy easy flipping, while Myles of Discs sees DX turn over, GStar flip up and Champion fade pretty aggressively. Takes split on how neutral it is: Robbie C Discgolf calls an old Champion copy incredibly neutral, while Bradley Martin finds a Champion copy very flippy and squirrelly into a headwind. Ben Howard DG finds it finishes harder than the MVP Trail when it does flip, and Brook Arnold finds the Discmania CD1 has slightly more wind control.

highlights.text: hyzer flips that ride flat and far

paras: Reviewers praise a controllable overstable fairway driver that turns a little and fades hard, with flat, stiff runs getting extra attention. Runs differ a lot: Myles of Discs finds the Eagle L holds straighter with more push, while the Eagle X fights out of the turn earlier and finishes harder, and Muddy Creek Production finds mellow Calvin Duo copies easier for slower arms than beefy Barsby and new Champion copies. Another Round Disc Golf calls the Calvin run a seven speed Innova Firebird that is crazy overstable when new, while Disc Golf Nerd finds a Star copy beefy but without the stand up and ride of a Champion Innova Firebird. Robbie C Discgolf likes that it has more extremes than an Innova TeeBird.

highlights.text: fights out of the turn earlier and finishes harder

paras: Reviewers praise a controllable, understable fairway driver that flips up from hyzer and holds anhyzer lines, with beginners and slower arms getting the most out of it. Plastic changes the disc: Bink Disc Golf finds a GStar copy far too flippy to throw while factory second Star and Halo Star copies handle fast arm speeds, and Reaper Discs credits Halo plastic with extra glide. Brook Arnold finds it a little less stable than the Axiom Crave, and Butterflight Disc Golf finds it slightly more understable and easier than the Latitude 64 River. Flight Path Disc Reviews warns that higher arm speeds can make it turn and burn into the ground.

highlights.text: turn and burn into the ground

paras: Reviewers praise an overstable approach putter that flies straight, fades gently and holds up in wind, especially inside about 225 feet. Plastic matters: Green Splatter advises gummy R-Pro and Star over rock hard DX and Champion, while Nick Carroll Disc Golf finds a DX copy kept its overstability for months and suits short crosswind putts. Brook Arnold finds it carries more glide through the fade than the MVP Stasis, and PaniniDG finds a Soft Pro goes a little straighter and farther than the Prodigy PA-1. Circles Edge Productions finds the domed top affects forehands and would prefer a flat topped copy.

highlights.text: flies straight, fades gently and holds up in wind
carries more glide through the fade

paras: Reviewers praise easy hyzer flips, glide and rollers for beginners and slower to middle arms. Plastic and weight split opinions: Reaper Discs finds Halo flies a little more overstable with more glide than Star, ChasinChains finds Halo more stable than rated, and DiscGolfMonkeys finds the light StarLite much less understable than expected. PoorBoy DiscGolf warns that hard throws turn it straight over into a roller, while Go Man Go Outdoors likens a GStar copy to an Innova Sidewinder that goes farther right. Brook Arnold gives it the win over the Discraft Avenger SS for understability and control.

highlights.text: easy hyzer flips, glide and rollers
hard throws turn it straight over into a roller

paras: Reviewers praise a dependable control driver that holds the line it is given and finishes left, good for woods shots and forehands. Runs and plastics differ: Fitzner Disc Golf finds the 2022 swirly Star run the flippiest and the 2021 run the most stable, and Disc Golf Examiner warns lower arm speeds may find new copies very overstable. Gladiator Disc Golf finds it carries forward on hyzer rather than dumping like an Innova Firebird, while DGweekly finds a GStar a touch less overstable and not quite as long as a Discmania PD. Hucking Aces calls it the perfect in between of the Innova Destroyer and the Innova TeeBird.

highlights.text: holds the line it is given
lower arm speeds may find new copies very overstable

paras: Reviewers praise a very predictable and controllable hybrid that flips up to flat on hyzers, holds anhyzers and finishes left, suiting beginners through pros. Many find it less overstable than the stated numbers: Part Time Disc Golf rates it closer to 6 4 0 2, and Daddy Delp Disc Golf finds it could be a little touchy, like a faster midrange. Gladiator Disc Golf places it between the Discraft Drone and the Innova Eagle in the bag, and Hucking Aces finds a profile and flight between the Innova TeeBird and the Innova Roc, with a finish left every single time.

highlights.text: less overstable than the stated numbers
a little touchy, like a faster midrange

paras: Reviewers praise the glide, easy hyzer flips to a straight finish and a comfortable feel, for slower to moderate arms and woods lines. Plastic changes a lot: one reviewer keeps the Neo as the version most true to its numbers and finds the Lux and Meta push straight before bigger, earlier fades, while another finds a new Neo straight and fairly overstable for slower arms until it is seasoned. DiscGolf Justice finds it slightly more stable than the Latitude 64 River, ChasinChains likes its more consistent flight over the Axiom Trance, and Flippy James Disc Golf prefers the Streamline Lift for forehands. One reviewer finds the Premier copy flippier than expected, and another warns that more power makes it roll over and burn.

highlights.text: easy hyzer flips to a straight finish
more consistent flight over the Axiom Trance
more power makes it roll over and burn

paras: Reviewers who like it praise the easy hyzer flips, the glide and the straight lines it holds in tight woods. Takes split on how far it turns: one reviewer sees flat throws stay straight the whole way, while others find flat throws very understable, and one says flat throws turn way over and almost roll. In The Bag Disc Golf compares its flight to the Kastaplast Göte but finds it smaller in hand. One reviewer rates its distance close to a putter's and would stick with a putter instead.

highlights.text: flat throws turn way over and almost roll

paras: Reviewers praise the distance, the hold in headwinds and a consistent hyzer finish, with forehand throws a common favorite. Plastic changes the disc more than usual: Neutron barely turns, Proton is slightly less stable, Plasma is straighter with less fade, and light Fission copies flip more easily but struggle in wind. Disc Golf Nerd places a Proton Photon between the Dynamic Discs Trespass and the Dynamic Discs Enforcer for stability, while TK Disc Golf finds a Fission copy flies like an older Star copy of the Innova Destroyer on flat power throws. One reviewer calls a Fission copy's overmold rim chipped and rough already, and another warns that arms under 55 to 60 mph will probably find a Neutron copy slightly overstable.

Reviewers like it as an easy, workable fairway driver for woods golf, hyzer flips and shots that finish right. Takes differ on a fresh copy: one reviewer sees more high speed stability than expected and says it needs some wear before it shows its full potential, while another sees flat throws turn before one fade. Jake from Disc Golf finds its late turn easier to hit than the Innova Leopard or the Latitude 64 River, though those probably have a little more glide. Noodle Arm Disc Golf sets it beside the Discmania FD as a bag foundation, and a stronger guest player likens it to the Innova Leopard and the MVP Inertia.

highlights.text: needs some wear before it shows its full potential

paras: Reviewers praise a straight, workable fairway driver that flips up on hyzers and finishes with a reliable fade. Plastic changes the feel: one reviewer finds an Eclipse copy a little more understable than most Servos, while another finds an Eclipse copy a smidge more stable than a Neutron Servo. Robbie C Discgolf picks it over the Axiom Crave for a little more turn and fight at the end, and Part Time Disc Golf says it takes a hard throw without flipping where the Axiom Crave probably would. One reviewer finds it dumps and stalls when nose up, and another traded a Neutron copy away for fading hard rather than carrying forward.

takes a hard throw without flipping
dumps and stalls when nose up
fading hard rather than carrying forward

paras: Reviewers praise a straight, glidy throwing putter that holds the angle it is released on, with hyzers flipping up to flat, for upshots, tunnels and wooded lines. One reviewer finds the Eclipse and Fission versions a little more stable and the Neutron and Plasma Soft versions flippier, though all go basically dead straight, while another blames the Plasma Soft for grip locks. Takes split on the MVP Glitch: Broderic. calls the Watt way flippier and less torque resistant than the MVP Glitch, while Cheating Lefty Disc Golf finds the heavier Watt handles more torque and wind. Drew Gibson finds the Watt flips up from hyzer to dead straight on touch shots where the MVP Ohm holds the hyzer and finishes left.

paras: Reviewers praise reliable overstability, strong wind resistance and a shallow, beadless rim that releases cleanly on forehand approaches. Plastic changes the feel: one reviewer finds the 400 and 500 copies by far the most overstable, while another sees the domier 400 float a little more and the flatter 300 fly shorter and more stable. Total Lefty Disc Golf finds it noticeably more overstable and a bit faster than the Discraft Zone but says it gets vertical and drops out of the sky, while Ben Howard DG finds it as overstable as the Discraft Zone OS with much more glide. Nate Turner expects the Prodigy A3 to hold a forehand shaping line a little better, and Matt White Disc Golf sees no clear performance edge between the two.

Reviewers like it as a point and shoot approach disc that holds its line and sits where it lands, with a shallower, more comfortable feel than the Kastaplast Berg. Takes differ on how it handles hyzers: one reviewer says it keeps pushing forward even on steep angles, while Luke Jenkins Disc Golf finds it flips up from a hyzer much more than a Kastaplast Berg. One reviewer says a release that is off line stays off line, and another finds it turns over and gets pushed around in a stiff headwind. Ben Howard DG sees the Kastaplast Berg hold up better in wind and says the Range flies like a normal throwing putter with a Kastaplast Berg feel.

highlights.text: holds its line and sits where it lands
a release that is off line stays off line
gets pushed around in a stiff headwind

paras: Reviewers praise a straight, glidey 11 speed that flips up on hyzers, handles wind and releases cleanly on forehands. Flight changes with plastic and weight: one reviewer finds the Neutron copy laser beam straight and the Proton copy about 40 feet longer but pulling right on flat releases, while another finds a lighter 168 gram copy drastically flippier on the same line. Disc Golf Puttheads compares it to the Innova Thunderbird, going 20 feet further, and to a seasoned Innova Wraith with less finish, and Daddy Disc Golf compares the flight to the MVP Tesla and places it near the MVP Photon. David Temple Disc Golf also finds it more stable than the MVP Zenith but sometimes too stable for the intended shot.

drastically flippier on the same line
sometimes too stable for the intended shot

paras: Reviewers praise the glide and easy hyzer flips, and many point it at beginners and slower arms. Plastic changes the flight: one reviewer finds a VIP-Ice copy holds the hyzer line while an Origio copy flattens, turns and keeps going right. Bradley Martin keeps it over the Discraft Meteor as a tad more stable with a little more glide, while Brook Arnold prefers the shallower Innova Fox because the Tursas has a deeper rim and taller dome that lead to grip lock. One reviewer calls it an understable beginner disc that stalls or stays on its side when ripped hard.

highlights.text: a tad more stable with a little more glide
stalls or stays on its side when ripped hard

paras: Reviewers praise a straight, gliding mid that holds whatever line it is thrown on, from beginners to experienced arms. Plastic matters: C-Line gets stiff in the cold and slippery when wet, and the new Italian blend and Swedish-made copies come out stable. Cheating Lefty Disc Golf and Andrew find forehands turn over or feel awkward. Apollo Disc Golf calls it the farthest throwing mid in the group, while Cole Bordis picks the Discraft Buzzz as more versatile.

highlights.text: holds whatever line it is thrown on
the farthest throwing mid in the group

paras: Reviewers like a comfortable, beadless mid that flies straight with a small hyzer flip and plenty of glide, and several recommend it for beginners and wooded courses. Stability depends on plastic and run: Disc Golf Deals USA finds FLX copies more understable and ESP more stable, while Andrew Wonch finds the newest Tour Series run quite a bit flippier. Disc Golf Nerd and Cheating Lefty Disc Golf both note that bigger arms get a turnover mid. Dropship Disc Golf places it between the Discraft Buzzz and the Discraft Meteor but struggles to predict whether it hyzers out or keeps turning.

highlights.text: struggles to predict whether it hyzers out

paras: Reviewers praise easy, glidy distance at low arm speeds and a disc that teaches hyzer flips, with several recommending it for beginners and slower arms. Takes split on stability: Six Sided Discs saw it fly overstable for a junior and laser straight for a smooth amateur, while Steven Cain (Cain Productions) found two copies staying quite stable. Cheating Lefty Disc Golf prefers the domier Heat backhand but recommends the Discraft Avenger SS overall, calling the Heat more finicky on forehands.

highlights.text: easy, glidy distance at low arm speeds

paras: Reviewers praise a comfortable bead, tacky plastics and a straight flight with a repeatable fade, and several use it for putts, upshots and short drives. Takes split on the bead and fade: Gladiator Disc Golf finds the big bead too tall to putt with, while GoHamDiscGolf says it fits the finger for any putting grip. Andrew finds it fades hard once it loses spin on longer putts. Swanky Disc Reviews finds the feel very close to the Prodigy PA-3, and Disc Golf Nerd likens the bead and rounded shape to the Dynamic Discs Judge.

highlights.text: fades hard once it loses spin

paras: Reviewers praise a comfortable, lower profile feel with a small bead, and a reliable flight that goes exactly where it is put. Plastic changes the flight a lot: Foundation Labs calls it shocking how much distance and stability change with plastic alone, and Stepwise Disc Golf found Star far more stable for headwinds than a beaten Champion Luster. Takes split on putting: JoeMamaGames dislikes it there as it is glidy and dinged out, while Stepwise Disc Golf and Foundation Labs both putt with it. Underground Sports likens the rounded profile and gummy feel to the Prodigy PA-3, and DGaiden finds it flies very similarly to the Discraft Luna but with less glide.

highlights.text: goes exactly where it is put

paras: Reviewers like a stable flight that holds its line and finishes left with a reliable bite at the end. Brook Arnold found it a good bit more stable than the Axiom Wrath, refusing to turn even when popped flat, and calls it maybe the closest thing to a Discmania PD thrown that was not one. Steven Kitchens Disc Golf warns it is very overstable despite its numbers and uses it for utility shots and big skips more than for distance. PoorBoy DiscGolf finds the flexible GStar plastic caught by light wind.

Reviewers like a reliable approach disc that lands flat near the basket and works well on forehands. Takes split on stability: Greybeard Disc Golf and Myles of Discs find the Proto Glow Nate Sexton Tour Series run a bit more stable than the Star, while Disc Golf Coolness finds the Rat probably the most understable of the Discraft Zone family and notes it has become more understable with use. Rodney Lane (DG Puttheads) expected an answer to the Discraft Zone or Westside Harp and found a comfortable, straight flying midrange for sidearm throwers instead. Myles of Discs finds it straighter than the Innova Toro, which flies similarly but is way more overstable.

Reviewers praise huge glide and easy distance for slower and moderate arms, with a range of plastics covering different stabilities. Frank B. finds Halo Star, Echo Star and Champion the more stable runs and finds GStar too flippy for forehands, while Disc Golf Nerd found a Star copy pretty stable and refusing to flip at full power. Cheating Lefty Disc Golf gives the Tern the win over the Discraft Hades for forgiveness and a finish that penetrates forward, while Brook Arnold says it flies like a beat-up Innova Destroyer but prefers the deeper Discmania DD for control. Brook Arnold and GoHamDiscGolf both find forehands hard to control.

Reviewers praise a reliable overstable approach disc with little glide that gives predictable distance and fights out of anhyzers. Most compare it to the Discraft Zone: ChasinChains and Bodanza Disc Golf find the two very similar, Apollo Disc Golf and Cole Bordis find the Toro a touch more overstable, and Frolfer Magazine (Adam W.) calls it more manipulable and forgiving. Takes split on feel: Bodanza Disc Golf likes the pinch grip, while Apollo Disc Golf dislikes the plus rim and Cole Bordis picks the Discraft Zone for the smaller rim. Reaper Discs and Disc Golf Nerd warn it is too beefy for brand new, low arm speed players.

Reviewers praise effortless glide, easy hyzer flips and a comfortable flight for beginners through medium arm speeds. Plastic matters: Cheating Lefty Disc Golf finds grippy K1 good when wet and suggests K1 Glow for wind, Matt White Disc Golf likes K1 Soft grip when wet but dislikes it on forehand, and Back of the Box Disc Golf found K1 Soft too floppy to grip well in summer heat. Daddy Delp Disc Golf likens the smooth, domey rim to a domier Dynamic Discs Maverick. Forehands and power throws draw criticism from several reviewers.

paras: Reviewers praise a very straight, glidey flight that holds the release line, with grippy Electron plastic. On comparisons, Apollo Disc Golf likens its flight to an Innova Aviar with a straighter, downward finish than the MVP Nomad, and Bodanza Disc Golf finds it a bit glidier than the MVP Nomad, which feels a little more overstable. Frolf Alliance Disc Golf calls it stable and controllable, sitting between the Axiom Envy and MVP Watt.

highlights.text: less for putting because of its depth

paras: Reviewers praise a very overstable, predictable fade that holds up in headwinds and out of anhyzer, with a shallow rim that many find good on forehands. Brook Arnold finds the finish stable like an Axiom Hex, but keeps the Streamline Echo, which turns over a little more and went a little further.

paras: Reviewers praise straight, controllable flights with a predictable fade, good glide and a small rim that suits many hand sizes. paras: Reviewers praise long, glidey, close to straight flights and plastic that several call among the nicest around. paras: Reviewers praise how it holds whatever line it is put on, with effortless glide, a comfortable rounded rim and soft Neutron plastic, for tight wooded gaps, jump putts and warm ups. paras: Reviewers praise a straight, neutral flight with a soft fade, plastic blends they rate highly, and use as both a putter and a point and shoot thrower. paras: Reviewers praise the straight, angle-controlled flight and K1 plastic that grips well. Andrew Wood Disc Golf replaced a beaten in Discraft Undertaker with it after it landed 25 to 30 feet farther on one hole, and Inside the Circle DG (Broden) found it more consistent and a little faster than the Latitude 64 Explorer. Discovering the World expected an Innova Valkyrie flight but found it closer to a Champion Innova Thunderbird. Runs differ: Cody Lehman found the 2020 tour run most stable and the 2021 and glow copies truer to the numbers, and a brand new copy can feel overstable.

highlights.text: a brand new copy can feel overstable

paras: Reviewers recommend it for beginners and slower arms because it turns over easily and glides, and some keep it for turnovers and tunnel shots even as their power grows. Foundation Labs called it a dependable understable disc that rolls easily from a flat throw, while Beaver Branch Disc Golf Adventures found it more understable than the Latitude 64 Jade, which holds up to more power. Green Splatter (Taylor Larsen) liked its slow, fading turnovers that the Innova Sidewinder or Innova Roadrunner often fight out of. Chain Raider Disc Golf found it turns and burns with any real power and felt mixed about bagging it.

highlights.text: turns and burns with any real power

paras: Reviewers praise the glide and a predictable flight that fades out, with plastics changing the stability: Disc Golf Examiner found Gold Line the most understable and Opto-X the most overstable. Bradley Martin compared it with the Innova Thunderbird and preferred the Innova Thunderbird for reliability without the worry of turning over, while Hucking Aces found two fresh copies slightly more overstable than the freshest Innova TeeBird. Beaver Branch Disc Golf Adventures found it nearly identical in flight to two Westside Bear copies. Faster arms and wind are the weak spots, since it turns more than wanted when hit hard.

highlights.text: turns more than wanted when hit hard

paras: Reviewers praise the straight, glidey flight and the grippy Electron and Proton feel, with most finding it holds whatever line it is put on. Takes split on putting: Level 2 Disc Golf sticks with MVP Atom for most putts because the deep dish does not suit, while Daddy Disc Golf finds it flies straighter with more glide than MVP Atom. TK Disc Golf sees it as a possible upgrade over MVP Ion for outside the circle putts. Too much power turns it over, and takes on headwinds differ.

highlights.text: holds whatever line it is put on
the deep dish does not suit
Too much power turns it over

paras: Reviewers like the straight push and hard, predictable finish, especially for forehand flick approaches and woods shots. Plastic matters: David Temple Disc Golf finds Electron glides the most, Neutron sits beefiest and Plasma skips more. Brook Arnold finds it more stable than Streamline Stabilizer, but nowhere near Discraft Zone OS, while Garry Patton prefers it to Streamline Stabilizer. Matt White Disc Golf probably will not bag it, preferring Axiom Envy for straight backhands and Prodigy A2 for overstable forehands.

highlights.text: straight push and hard, predictable finish

paras: Reviewers praise a straight flight with a dependable fade, and a grippy feel that suits putts and upshots. Bradley Martin prefers it over MVP Atom for long putts thanks to a straighter flight, though finds it slower and less glidy. TK Disc Golf finds Electron super grippy and notes lighter copies turn a little more, while a soft Neutron copy runs a bit more stable. Headwinds are the weak spot, since it can turn over.

highlights.text: straight flight with a dependable fade

paras: Reviewers praise the straight, torque resistant flight and the comfortable flat top, especially on forehands and in wind. Takes split on stability by plastic: IceBerg TV finds Electron fairly neutral and Proton much beefier, while Disc Golf Deals USA finds Neutron fades most. Disc Golf Nerd likens it to a longer, faster Axiom Envy, but Daddy Delp Disc Golf finds much less distance than MVP Reactor or Axiom Hex. Chris Goodrich calls it moderately overstable, not in the class of MVP Deflector or Axiom Pyro.

Reviewers like it for hyzer flips, wooded turnovers and easy glide, and several would hand it to newer players. Takes split on how far it turns: Brook Arnold finds it more understable than MVP Detour, while Ben Howard DG finds so much late stability that it will not hold a turnover line, and dropped it from the bag. TK Disc Golf prefers it over Axiom Paradox for moderate arms because it is more controllable, while DBW Disc Golf notes the Axiom Paradox holds its turn the whole flight. Jake from Disc Golf likens it to a slightly faster, farther Innova Mako3.

highlights.text: hyzer flips, wooded turnovers and easy glide
will not hold a turnover line

paras: Reviewers praise the comfortable feel, the glide and how well it holds a line, from hyzer flips to long anhyzers. Takes split on stability: GoHamDiscGolf calls it the most understable midrange in the Prodigy lineup, similar to Discraft Buzzz SS, while IceBerg TV finds the ReBlend a power player's disc, closer to Prodigy M3 than a flip up. Brook Arnold finds a new 400 copy fades more, and kept Innova Roc3 in the bag. Disc Golf Nerd finds it flies much like Discraft Buzzz, so it may not earn a spot.

highlights.text: how well it holds a line

paras: Reviewers like the shaped lines, from hyzer flips that ride straight to anhyzers that push without dumping. Plastic is the big split: Erik G finds an older Eclipse run flies nothing like its numbers, much like Innova Thunderbird, while Shea Stevens finds the Eclipse almost like MVP Terra and not for the bag. Matt Dollar Disc Golf finds the Neutron more stable than Axiom Insanity, and Garry Patton likens the slot to an MVP Matrix that goes further.
