Reviewers like the easy flip to flat and the glide, and see it as a good first fairway driver for slower arms. Takes split on how flippy it is: Disc Golf Examiner finds a big arm turns it over and never comes out of the turn, while Disc Golf Nerd finds it less flippy than Innova Mamba and flying really straight. PoorBoy DiscGolf plans to swap the VIP Air copy in for Latitude 64 Jade, which shares its numbers, and GoHamDiscGolf calls Westside Underworld much more understable. Disc Golf Nerd adds that the big dome top is not for everyone.

highlights.text: easy flip to flat and the glide
a big arm turns it over
big dome top is not for everyone

paras: Reviewers praise the straight flight, the glide and the familiar domed rim, and several call it an underrated midrange. Chris Goodrich finds it the least overstable, straightest and glidiest of four midranges that include Innova Roc, Discraft Buzzz and an older Dynamic Discs Truth. Foundation Labs likens it to the feel of Innova Roc with the flight of Discraft Buzzz, maybe a hair less stable, while Trilogy Talk finds the Tournament fades very little and the Hybrid is clearly more overstable. Part Time Disc Golf finds it gains distance over Dynamic Discs EMac Truth with a power grip, but has no edge on a fan grip.

highlights.text: the least overstable, straightest and glidiest
no edge on a fan grip

paras: Reviewers praise a very understable mid that flips up to flat at low power and gives a wide range of utility shots, from hyzer flips to rollers. Takes split on fit: some call it a teacher for beginners and angle control, while others say it can flip too much on some course shots or needs special lines to fly as wanted. Disc Golf Deals USA ranks it in the middle for stability, between Discmania Founder and Discraft Archer, and calls its anhyzer shot almost identical to Innova Rollo. Bodanza Disc Golf finds it flips faster than Latitude 64 Fuse and keeps turning with zero fade.

highlights.text: flips up to flat at low power
flip too much on some course shots
needs special lines to fly as wanted

paras: Reviewers like an easy, gliding mid that flips up on hyzer and turns gently on flat throws, and some call it a good tool for learning hyzer flips. Takes split on stability: Deej Disc Golf finds the Kyle Klein glow C-Line flippier than listed and throws Axiom Hex better, while Nate Turner finds it more flippy than Discmania MD1 and good for beginners. Plastic and run matter too, since Neo and soft Exo hold the turn, Meta fights back after turning, and a first Midnight Prowl run flies much more understable than the second. IceBerg TV has not had as much fun with a neutral mid since MVP Detour.

highlights.text: good tool for learning hyzer flips

paras: Reviewers praise a smooth, straight fairway driver that holds a hyzer, flips up and glides well, and a couple call it good for slower arm speeds and finesse players. Takes split on wear and angle: one reviewer finds it gets too flippy once it beats in, another finds it hard to bring back once turning, and a third says it rolls over with a bit too much angle. Part Time Disc Golf ranks it in the middle for stability, between Discraft Scorch and Discraft Thrasher, while Kyle Eberdt - Disc Golf picks it over Discraft Cicada, finding it pushes a little farther. Robbie C Discgolf finds it goes a little farther than Discraft Stalker and flies very similar to MVP Servo.

highlights.text: too flippy once it beats in

paras: Reviewers praise a far-flying, workable mid that holds whatever angle it is thrown on and finishes with a dependable fade. Takes split on stability and plastic: Cheating Lefty Disc Golf finds Fuzion the most understable, a lighter Lucid much more understable and Lucid X very overstable, while Andrew guesses stiff Lucid might be slightly more overstable than a looser Fuzion version. ChasinChains finds it a more stable, slightly glidier Discraft Buzzz that does not flip up at all on baby hyzers, and Cory Lesniak (IAmViktor13) moved to it from Discraft Buzzz wanting more glide. Fergie4rlz, a natural hyzer thrower, finds Westside Warship flips to flat much easier.

highlights.text: does not flip up at all on baby hyzers

paras: Reviewers praise an overstable fairway driver with a flat top feel and a surprising amount of glide, a staple for forehands and wind that must not turn over. Takes split on stability by plastic and age: Apollo Disc Golf finds Hybrid X sits between Lucid and Lucid X, Ben Propes finds the new German Lucid blend much more overstable than the old one, and DiscGolf Justice says a beat-in copy loses some stability and confidence. Disc Golf Deals USA finds a team series Lucid flies noticeably straighter than a usual Felon and picks Dynamic Discs Maverick as the better disc of the day. Part Time Disc Golf finds it holds a straight line longer than Discmania Splice, and Bodanza Disc Golf finds it flies close to Innova Firebird and Discraft Raptor.

highlights.text: flat top feel and a surprising amount of glide
beat-in copy loses some stability and confidence
holds a straight line longer than Discmania Splice

paras: Reviewers praise a comfortable, flat overstable midrange that works in wind, suits forehand and fades back no matter what, though some call it a disc for intermediate to advanced players. Takes split on how overstable it is: Just Run It - Disc Golf finds the fade weaker than the flight numbers suggest and would probably pick Innova Gator for more stability, while JustDisc finds it has more fade than Innova Gator and calls it a wonderful disc that trumps it. Montreal Disc Golf finds the Star weirdly more overstable than the Champion, and Great Lakes Disc notes a no bead bottom unlike Innova Gator. Disc Store finds it significantly more overstable than Innova Rat but says it does not go far.

highlights.text: fade weaker than the flight numbers suggest

paras: Reviewers praise a flippy, high-gliding mid that is easy to turn over and carries far with little effort, with several calling it a good fit for newer players and slower arms. Takes split on plastic and weight: Disc Zone finds Halo Star a tad more stable and straighter than Star, Six Sided Discs finds Halo Star flipped over quickly, and Disc Golf Nerd finds the lighter copy touchy and easy to flip by accident. ChasinChains finds it a click or two flippier than MVP Detour, while Robbie C Discgolf finds it significantly flippier than Discraft Malita and gives the Malita the edge in hand feel and shot shaping. Disc Golf Nerd finds it more straight to neutral than Innova Rollo, which is quicker and touchier.

highlights.text: touchy and easy to flip by accident

paras: Reviewers mostly praise it as a dependable overstable midrange that holds straight for a stretch before a hard fade, with several saying it handles headwind and forehand flex shots well. Takes split on feel and stability: one reviewer finds a glow Champion copy uncomfortable thrown flat and prone to diving in wind, while another calls the Star copy fast and stable rather than super overstable. Low glide keeps it a short range tool, and bead size and dome vary between copies. Disc Golf Nerd finds a Champion copy less overstable than the Dynamic Discs Justice and more overstable than the Prodigy A3.

highlights.text: Low glide keeps it a short range tool

paras: Reviewers praise it as an easy hyzer flip and roller disc that works at slow arm speeds and suits beginners learning to flip discs. Takes split on how far it is useful: one reviewer calls it a complete roller disc for intermediates, while another plays a full round with it, finds it needs a lot of touch and says it stays unused in the bag. Halo copies hold straighter lines than Star or Champion, though all of them overturn when thrown hard. Disc Golf Deals USA finds the Rollo a little more stable than the Discmania Founder, though the Founder rolls more easily.

highlights.text: easy hyzer flip and roller disc

paras: Reviewers describe it as a straight fairway driver that holds its line and finishes with a fade, and one praises how it behaves in headwind and crosswind. Takes split on stability: one reviewer finds a Halo copy more overstable than its numbers suggest and treats it as a utility disc, while another calls it a touch more stable than the Discraft Passion with a bit more fade. Brook Arnold picks the TL3 over the Discraft Passion for consistency, while ChasinChains gives the TL3 a four to two win in a six hole challenge but notes it will not turn like the Passion.

highlights.text: will not turn like the Passion

paras: Reviewers mostly praise it as a putter that works for putts and short approaches, with a small bead, good glide and a flight that holds a hyzer line. Takes split on feel and plastic: one reviewer finds the soft Electron prone to grip lock on release, while another likes it more for throwing than putting because it does not feel right for a putt. Nick Carroll Disc Golf finds it a touch more stable in a crosswind than the Axiom Pixel and functionally almost identical, and Infinite Discs finds it putts very like the Dynamic Discs Judge. Brook Arnold finds the stability close to the Discmania P2.

highlights.text: works for putts and short approaches
prone to grip lock on release

paras: Reviewers mostly describe it as an overstable approach disc that sits close to the Discraft Zone, with a little more glide and stability and a thin bead that helps forehand grip. Takes split on forehand and wind: one reviewer finds it holds a forehand line a little better than the Prodigy A2, while another finds it too stable for a forehand flex shot. Andrew finds it sits between the Discraft Zone and the MVP Deflector in stability, with a little more bite in wind than the Zone. Bodanza Disc Golf finds it flies lower and more driven than the Prodigy A4, with much less glide, and says it held up worse in wind than the Prodigy A2.

highlights.text: too stable for a forehand flex shot

paras: Reviewers mostly praise it as a versatile fairway driver for turnovers, hyzer flips and woods shots that suits beginners and lower arm speeds. Takes split on stability: plastic and wear change it a lot, with Chameleon described as the more stable, VIP in the middle and a beat in copy very flippy, and one reviewer finds it less usable as arm speed rises. Dustin Mouret finds it flips more than the Discmania FD and sits a bit less stable than the Discraft Passion, and Beaver Branch Disc Golf Adventures finds it fades more than the Latitude 64 River. Part Time Disc Golf says it flies with regular stability, kind of like the Innova TeeBird, in the woods with little wind or in a tailwind.

highlights.text: less usable as arm speed rises

paras: Reviewers mostly describe it as a flippy distance driver that suits medium to slower arm speeds and works as a stepping stone to faster discs. Takes split on stability: Orbit and flat VIP copies run very flippy, while VIP Air and Tournament-X run stable, and one reviewer is on the fence because flights vary so much from one plastic or run to the next. Daddy Delp Disc Golf found a VIP-X more stable than wanted, with less distance than the Latitude 64 Rive, while IceBerg TV compares a stable domey copy to the Innova Destroyer.

Reviewers praise a very overstable driver that fights out of anhyzer, and one finds it holds its line in wind. Russell Disc Golf finds it flies more like an Innova Firebird than an Innova Thunderbird, while Pete Collins Disc Golf finds it very close to the Innova Thunderbird but a touch less overstable, flatter and less domey. TBH Disc Golf calls the prototype a beefier MVP Tesla that gives up distance because it has no turn.

highlights.text: gives up distance because it has no turn

paras: Reviewers call it a stable, predictable putter that glides well and breaks in nicely, with the bead taking the wear. Most dislike the slick, stiff plastic: one found it brittle enough to split after a tree hit, others lose grip or release consistency, and putting results are mixed. Disc Golf Puttheads finds it much more stable than a regular Innova Aviar and like a Gateway Wizard in upshots, while IceBerg TV finds it glides farther than the more stable Gateway Wizard.

Reviewers praise a glidey, understable fairway driver that is easy to throw and suits slower to medium arm speeds and beginners. Reviewers split on the rim and forehands: one reviewer finds the bulgy rim comfortable and forehands easy, while another calls the rim bulbous and forehands poor, with rollers the likely result. Nick Carroll Disc Golf finds it closer to the Innova Leopard than the Innova Roadrunner, gains about 10 to 15 feet over the Innova Leopard, and bagged it in place of the Innova Leopard3. One reviewer finds GStar gummier and a tick more understable than Champion.

Reviewers use it for approaches, putts and some drives, and one finds it glidier than expected with some bite at the end. Takes split on stability: one calls it very overstable and definitely an approach disc, while another finds the baseline plastic pretty flippy, with no fade on some throws, and a third flips it over on a forehand flick. Cam Hoff DG finds it very overstable like a Discraft Zone and says the Westside Tursas stays the group favorite over the Innova Shark. Plastic notes are mixed: DX felt a bit gummier than usual, while baseline plastic felt fake and light.

Reviewers mostly praise it as a flippy, glidey fairway driver that flips up from a hyzer and holds anhyzer lines through the whole flight. Takes split on how much turn is too much, since a second thrower found it too flippy for their angles, and one reviewer finds Orbit plastic flies close to Grand with little added stability. Disc Golf Deals USA calls it very similar to the Latitude 64 Grace, just a little slower. Part Time Disc Golf believes it is slightly less stable than the Latitude 64 Sweep, with the Latitude 64 Rive the most stable of the three.

highlights.text: very similar to the Latitude 64 Grace

paras: Reviewers mostly describe it as a Latitude 64 Pure with a bead, a little more stable, and a good fit for slower arms as a throwing putter. Takes split on putting, since some love the depth and feel while others find it too deep or too rounded over to love for putting. Disc Golf Deals USA says it flies like a Latitude 64 Pure but a bit more stable, and Part Time Disc Golf finds it less stable than the Prodigy PA-3, turning over better and holding the turn. Bodanza Disc Golf prefers the Latitude 64 Pure and finds the bead adds only a little stability.

highlights.text: a Latitude 64 Pure with a bead
too rounded over to love for putting

paras: Reviewers like the hand feel and rim profile, and find the flight stable and fairly neutral, suited to stronger arms. Takes differ on plastic, since BaseGrip flips up quickly and one finds it too stiff for a driver, while DuraFlex gets good flex lines on a lot of hyzer angle. Whyzer Productions finds the flight super similar to the Prodigy D3 and the feel close to the Prodigy X3, and J3 Disc Golf finds it flies like a beaten-in Prodigy D3.

highlights.text: flies like a beaten-in Prodigy D3

paras: Reviewers mostly praise it as a straight putter that holds whatever line it goes on, with a good hyzer hold at low speed. BaseGrip is reported as a little straighter than DuraFlex, though one finds the BaseGrip plastic surprisingly stiff and slick. Vegan Disc Golfer finds it less understable than a Prodigy PA-4, and Whyzer Productions finds it holds the angle it is thrown on where the Prodigy PA-4 always turns. Disc Golf Reviewer finds the flat top slightly less comfortable and would pick the Discraft Luna for consistency.

highlights.text: holds whatever line it goes on

paras: Reviewers praise the straight push, the dependable fade in wind and a shallow rim that sits well on forehand. Variety Disc Golf calls it way more overstable than expected, with a flight pretty similar to the Axiom Pyro, while Disc Golf Over 40 found the Neutron version flew straighter and less overstable than the Axiom Pyro on most throws. Garry Patton expects it to replace the MVP Reactor when the wind is up, and Swanky Disc Reviews finds the prototype very overstable for a backhand thrower, maybe a little less than the MVP Deflector.

highlights.text: very overstable for a backhand thrower

paras: Reviewers praise how far it goes and how workable it is on hyzer flips, anhyzers and flat shots, with tunnel and wooded lines a favorite. Takes split on stability: ChainTheoryDG finds the Neutron turns for most of a flat release, like a slightly more stable Axiom Rhythm, while Disc Golf Deals USA finds the pre-release version less stable than the Discmania FD on most lines. Zach Turpin Disc Golf places it between the Axiom Crave and the MVP Servo and is disappointed that it sits so close to both.

highlights.text: hyzer flips, anhyzers and flat shots

paras: Reviewers praise the distance and glide, and the retooled Neutron run for a flatter, more comfortable shoulder and a flight that holds turn. Plastic is the main split: Part Time Disc Golf calls the 157 g Fission very flippy and the 167 g the most reliable, while IceBerg TV finds a later Neutron run less stable than the prototype but still really stable. Flying Fajita Disc Golf finds the Fission turns about as much out of the box as a beaten-in Innova Destroyer, and David Temple Disc Golf found it going a little farther than the MVP Photon at three weights.

Reviewers praise the glide and a disc that holds a line into wind, with a pop-top dome and a late fade. Takes differ by run and dome: Nate Turner finds the Horizon version too much disc for some shorter holes, while Calculated Disc Golf puts the third Eagle McMahon run between a very flippy first run and a fading Horizon run. OTB Discs finds it far more overstable late in the flight than the Discmania DD3, while Apollo Disc Golf finds a later run flies like a slightly understable Innova Destroyer when thrown with enough arm speed.

highlights.text: too much disc for some shorter holes

paras: Reviewers praise a controllable, straight flight that fights wind, mostly in S-Line plastic. Plastic is the main split: Apollo Disc Golf finds the stock S-Line copies more stable than the Horizon version, which is significantly flippier, and Dustin Mouret - Disc Golf found the first stock S-Line run more overstable than the Horizon one. DiscGolf Justice found the S-Line DD1 surprisingly more stable than the Discmania DD3, while DeuZ Disc Golf found the Horizon DD1 on par with an Innova Wraith while the Latitude 64 Grace went farther.

highlights.text: controllable, straight flight that fights wind

paras: Reviewers praise a dependable overstable nine-speed that flies straighter than its reputation, with a comfortable forehand feel. Runs and plastic are the main split: Nate Turner found three FD3 runs flew clearly apart in stability, Zach The Discmaniac finds the Open Color Glow run one of the most overstable thrown, and Part Time Disc Golf found the Glow run too beefy for their arm speed. Disc Zone found a Horizon run only a touch more overstable than the S-Line and flying much like an Innova Firebird or a Discraft Raptor.

highlights.text: too beefy for their arm speed

paras: Reviewers praise how far and easily it glides, with a flatter top and a stiffer, tougher plastic. Takes split on where it earns a spot: Masters Line Disc Golf found it the strongest performer for distance among four understable discs, including the Latitude 64 Diamond, Prodigy F9 and DGA Vortex, while Broderic. sees it as a fun, get-out-of-trouble disc more than a practical one. Chains on Tap prefers it to an older Innova Archangel for the flatter top and tougher plastic.

highlights.text: how far and easily it glides

paras: Reviewers praise a stable mid that rides the line it is thrown on, with a flat profile that sits comfortably on forehand. Takes split on the forehand: Brook Arnold finds it still wobbles and flips up while flying a touch straighter and glidier than the Discmania Method, while Arrebarre calls it straighter and more point and shoot than the Method. Big Guy Little Disc finds it clearly more stable than a Discraft Buzzz but not as flat as the Axiom Balance, and Gravyboi Disc Golf finds the prototype flips quicker than the Discmania MD4 and fades harder.

highlights.text: rides the line it is thrown on

paras: Reviewers praise a shallow, grippy putter that goes straight, holds hyzer and anhyzer lines and handles forehand torque. Takes split on stability: Desert Trek Media finds it has far more flip than the Discmania Sensei, while IceBerg TV calls it stable and point and shoot. Apollo Disc Golf argues it is a better Discraft Luna for most players, and Peachy Disc Golf leans toward the MVP Watt for the bag.

Reviewers praise the distance and a long, held turn, best for slower arms. Takes split on stability: IceBerg TV finds it clearly more stable than the typical stock Q-Line DD1, while Club51 DG finds it too flippy to bag and Bodanza Disc Reviews finds it hard to throw with power without burning over. Disc Zone finds it a full notch flippier than the Innova Wraith, and Dice Hyzer Disc Golf calls it as understable as the Innova Mamba without the roller risk.

Reviewers praise how far it goes and how well it glides, with a little more push than a regular fairway FD. Takes split on stability: some find it too stable and beefy for an FD, while others found it flew about the same as older FDs at easy power. Deej Disc Golf found it more stable than the regular Discmania FD and closer to a 7 6 0 2, and Club51 DG found a little more push and glide than an older S-Line Discmania FD. IceBerg TV found a red run much straighter than an earlier blue run that was unthrowably overstable.

highlights.text: too stable and beefy for an FD
a little more push and glide

paras: Reviewers like how easily it flips and turns, with one calling the glide insane and another calling it a utility, super flip disc. Takes split on stability: one copy held its line without flipping, while another cut and rolled when thrown too hard. Oklahyzer Disc Golf found it feels more like a fast mid-range than a driver and compared it with Discraft SoL, picking it as the favorite for hand feel, while IceBerg TV compared the rim width to Axiom Crave but found it turns far more.

highlights.text: how easily it flips and turns
cut and rolled when thrown too hard

paras: Reviewers praise it as a beginner-friendly distance driver, with tremendous glide and a flight that flips up to flat and finishes straight or with a gentle fade. Takes split on who it suits: it is pitched at players learning a first distance driver, but also at players a year or two in who want a mid-distance turnover shot. Cheating Lefty Disc Golf found it holds a hyzer line better than Discraft Heat and flies straight longer, though Discraft Heat is easier for turnovers, while Great Lakes Disc found quite a bit more turn than Innova Sidewinder. Swanky Disc Golf called Prodigy X3 a longer, more stable version, and found a beat-in copy hangs hard to the right.

Reviewers mostly describe it as a stable throwing putter that fills a gap between Discraft Luna and Discraft Zone, with a putter feel and a late finish. Takes split on how it compares with Discraft Zone SS: Deej Disc Golf found it a touch more stable, while Ozark Mountain Discs found it nothing like it and Bodanza Disc Reviews called it a consistently overstable putter version of Discraft Zone SS. Forehand is the weak spot, as several reviewers found the rounded rim less secure or prone to turning over with wobble. Easy Game Disc Golf would not swap Discraft Zone SS out of the bag for it and found a beaten-in Discraft Zone could do the same jobs.

highlights.text: fills a gap between Discraft Luna

paras: Reviewers praise how easily it flips up to flat and holds a turnover line, with plenty of glide for a 7-speed disc. Flight varies by plastic and run, and Flying Fajita Disc Golf ranked it as more understable than Discraft Passion, Discraft Cigarra and Discraft Athena after finding one run ridiculously understable and another really overstable. Deej Disc Golf found it extremely similar to Axiom Crave and Cheating Lefty Disc Golf found it a little more understable than Axiom Rhythm at slower speeds, while Masters Line Disc Golf found it tighter in spread but shorter than Kastaplast Falk at every arm speed. Flat forehands can burn over, and some found it flippier than the listed numbers.

highlights.text: how easily it flips up to flat

paras: Reviewers praise the straight, controllable flight and comfortable rim, with several liking it for wind and wooded holes. Takes split on stability, with one reviewer finding it dead straight with nothing turning over and another finding it a lot flippier than imagined in ESP. Ben Callaway found it more stable than Discraft Cicada but still touchy, placing it between Discraft Cicada and Discraft Athena, while Zach Turpin Disc Golf called it basically a faster Discraft Luna. Bodanza Disc Golf found it a tiny bit slower than Discraft Athena and heard that the ESP version flips more than the Z.

Reviewers mostly describe a fairly straight flight with a dependable fade and good distance. Takes split on how far it goes: Adam Hammes found it goes as far as some Discraft Nuke copies with little effort, while Peachy Disc Golf found it shortest of a group that included Discraft Zeus and Discraft Hades at a low arm speed. Swanky Disc Golf found it went further than Innova Wraith despite flying more overstable, while ChasinChains preferred Discmania Enigma, which has more glide and flips up easier. Jose Sanchez found it pushes straighter than Latitude 64 Grace.

highlights.text: as far as some Discraft Nuke copies
found it shortest of a group

paras: Reviewers mostly describe a very overstable driver that holds a hyzer line, fades out and does well in headwinds, best for players with faster arms. PoorBoy DiscGolf found it feels like a slightly less overstable Discraft Nuke, while Foundation Disc Golf found it less overstable than expected and close to how Innova Destroyer flies. DiscGolfology found it flies and feels the same as the retooled Discraft Venom, and Bradley Martin heard the other player call it nearly the same disc as Dynamic Discs Enforcer. Reaper Discs heard it flies like Discraft Zeus or Innova Destroyer without the high-speed turn, but found it goes far only for the top one percent of arm speeds.

highlights.text: top one percent of arm speeds

paras: Reviewers praise the straight, glidey flight and the smaller, more comfortable feel in the hand, though extra power can make it inconsistent and prone to turning over. Takes split on where it sits: Matt Hester Disc Golf found almost the same flight as Discraft Buzzz SS and was unsure it earns a bag spot, Disc Golf Reviewer placed it between Discraft Buzzz and Discraft Buzzz SS, and Disc Zone found it goes farther than Discraft Buzzz and is not understable at all. Zach Turpin Disc Golf found it extremely close to Discraft Buzzz and shaped like Discmania MD1. Disc Golf Puttheads found it just a hair more stable than Innova Fox, and ChasinChains slightly preferred it over Discraft Joy.

highlights.text: extra power can make it inconsistent
unsure it earns a bag spot

paras: Reviewers say it goes very far for strong arms, with one finding it went farthest of a group of 13-speeds and another getting a big anhyzer that fought out the whole way. Takes split on the rim and stability: some find the big, deep rim uncomfortable and harder to grip on forehand, while Bodanza Disc Reviews liked the hand feel. Bodanza Disc Reviews found it a good bit less stable than Discmania DD4, and Bodanza Disc Golf found it went farther than Kastaplast Guld. Disc Golf Reviewer found it needs serious power and compared the power it needs to Innova Ape.

highlights.text: goes very far for strong arms

paras: Reviewers who loved it praise a Raptor that is overstable without dumping and still has glide, with the Z FLX version favored for sitting where it lands instead of skipping. Takes split on stability: Luce Disc Golf found the Z Raptor flipped up more than the Innova Firebird and Discmania FD3 for a little extra distance, and Luke Jenkins Disc Golf found the Z Swirl copy flippier than hoped. Six Sided Discs found the Raptor holds a similar line to the Innova Firebird and matched its distance, while DiscGolfology called it nearly the same mold as the Discmania FD3.

highlights.text: flipped up more than the Innova Firebird

paras: Reviewers praise an easy flipping distance driver that goes far without much power, suiting slower arm speeds and players learning hyzer flips and turnovers. Plastic changes the flight: Cheating Lefty Disc Golf found the Big Z the most understable but not one for headwinds, the Z the straightest and newer ESP runs considerably more overstable, while Disc Golf Nerd found the ESP the most understable and the Big Z the farthest. Part Time Disc Golf paired it with the more stable Discraft Scorch for most distance drives, and Baysinger's Disc Golf Channel had one tester compare the lighter first run Z copy's flight to the Latitude 64 River.

Reviewers who liked it describe a workhorse fairway driver that holds its line in a headwind and finishes with a reliable fade, suiting newer players moving up to nine speed as well as experienced ones. Takes split on consistency: Brook Arnold found a Titanium copy beefier than earlier ones yet still sometimes rolling over, and Andrew Wood Disc Golf found a long-used Titanium copy had become flippy. Tickling Chains Disc Golf found the ESP flew almost identically to the Innova Savant, and Disc Golf Reviewer compared it to the Innova TeeBird, though a touch beefier and faster.

highlights.text: holds its line in a headwind

paras: Reviewers who liked it call it a straighter, less overstable take on the Discraft Zone that suits short approaches and controlled forehands, with a thin feel in the hand. Takes split on consistency: ChasinChains found forehands finicky, with any wobble making it turn over, and Pure Flight Disc Golf found low glide and a wish to drop early in wind. Ozark Mountain Discs found it noticeably straighter than the Discraft Zone, IceBerg TV placed it between the Discraft Luna and the Discraft Zone, and Disc Golf Deals USA found it turns where the Axiom Tempo does not.

highlights.text: noticeably straighter than the Discraft Zone

paras: Reviewers praise a very overstable utility mid that comes out of an anhyzer, fights a headwind and feels comfortable on forehands. The main drawback is reach: Beaver Branch Disc Golf Adventures got about 260 feet against 272 and 300 for the Dynamic Discs Verdict, and Bradley Martin found it carried noticeably shorter than the Discraft Buzzz OS. LJ Disc Golf found it carried farther than the Discmania Mutant on hyzer shots, and DiscGolf Justice found it more comfortable than the Discmania Mutant. Plastic matters a little: Andrew found a Fluid copy a bit less stable than Lucid, and Disc Golf Nerd found Lucid-X firmer and more overstable than regular Lucid.

Reviewers who liked it call the Berg X a beefier Kastaplast Berg that handles forehand power and fades more reliably, suiting forehand throwers and players who want more fade as the Kastaplast Berg wears. Takes split on how big the change is: Swanky Disc Golf called the difference subtle and often hard to notice, while Tips Från Coachen found it clearly a more stable disc that holds up better in a headwind than the Kastaplast Berg. Broderic. found it much more overstable with less glide than the Kastaplast Berg, pushing straight on a flex line like the Discraft Zone OS, and called it a crutch for newer players inside 200 feet.

highlights.text: subtle and often hard to notice

paras: Reviewers who liked it describe a controllable, glidy seven speed that flies straight with a dependable fade and suits players across skill levels. Takes split on stability: Disc Golf Deals USA and Bodanza Disc Golf found the K1 Glow and K1 Grind copies flippy, while Bad Throws Good Bros Disc Golf found a stable TeeBird flight that never flipped up. Russell Disc Golf called it a clone of the Innova TeeBird and Innova Eagle, and Tips Från Coachen found it went farther than the Innova TeeBird, putting that down to its small turn.

highlights.text: went farther than the Innova TeeBird

paras: Reviewers who loved it call the Compass a controllable mid-range with glide and a comfortable feel, and one uses it on probably every hole. Takes split on stability: Rec Rob found it more stable than the Dynamic Discs EMac Truth and a great headwind fighter, while DGweekly found it less stable than hoped, close to the Dynamic Discs Truth, and suggested more overstability for windy shots. Fergie4rlz found it a bit more stable than the Latitude 64 Fuse, and Flying Fajita Disc Golf became convinced it has the exact same flight as the Thought Space Athletics Pathfinder. Plastic matters too: No Hassle Disc Golf found the gummy Frost turned more than Gold.

Reviewers who loved it praise a stable 13 speed that carries far, fades dependably and handles forehand torque, in a grippy plastic that feels great. Takes split on how overstable it is: Swanky Disc Golf thought it perhaps not quite as overstable as the numbers suggest, while Victor Folcke found the first throws really overstable and kept fighting left. Chris Goodrich found a flight very similar to the Dynamic Discs Raider, with the Rive turning over a bit more and landing five to ten feet farther, and IceBerg TV believed it a little faster and more overstable than the Latitude 64 Grace. Arm speed is the catch, with Beaver Branch Disc Golf Adventures saying their arm tops out around a speed 12.

Reviewers who loved it describe a flat topped overstable driver that feels good on forehands, fights wind and holds its line before an early fade. Takes split on the Trail pairing: Decent Disc Golf found it much more stable than expected and was not sold because it does what other discs in the bag already do, while Luke Jenkins Disc Golf called the MVP Trail and Control a perfect driver pair. DarthYodah Disc Golf found it beefier than the Discmania PD off the tee with more push, though it skips a long way after landing, and Disc Golf Deals USA thought it was the PD that fans have been looking for. TBH Disc Golf found it fades earlier and goes shorter than the MVP Trail on backhands.

Reviewers praise it as an overstable approach putter that holds a line, fights out of anhyzer and sits down close to the basket with almost no glide. Takes split on how overstable it is, with some calling it somewhat overstable and others clearly overstable once thrown harder, while forehands go smoothly for some and wobble on very hard throws for others. ADK Discs found it slightly more overstable than the Streamline Range, and Bodanza Disc Reviews found it flew much like the Kastaplast Berg X but went a little farther. Distance is the main limit, with long backhand hyzer and flat throws coming up short.

highlights.text: sits down close to the basket

paras: Reviewers praise it as a fast, controllable driver that stays stable and glides far, even in lightweight AIR plastic. Takes differ on stability: one found a heavier Spectrum Air copy flipping up to flat, another called it stable but not super overstable, and a first-run prototype reportedly flew overstable with extra distance. One reviewer found an earlier 300 Glimmer run too flat and too stable to go far enough.

highlights.text: too flat and too stable to go far enough

paras: Reviewers suggest it for players with a slow, smooth release who want a disc that flips early, and see it as a good tool for learning hyzer flips. Takes split on control: a large dome sinks into the fingers and sends forehands out nose down for one reviewer, while another found it holds the turn all the way at about 80 percent power and burns over at full power. Brook Arnold found the MVP Signal the more controllable disc and likened the F9 flight to the Discmania Function, and Masters Line Disc Golf found it the flippiest of four understable discs on paper but not the distance winner, against the Latitude 64 Diamond, Discmania Function and DGA Vortex.

Reviewers praise it as an understable, glidey throwing putter that flips up from a hyzer and works for turnovers and tight lines through gaps or woods. Takes split on how flippy it is: one reviewer found it not as flippy as its reputation suggests and better as a putter, while another found it flippy enough to need extra hyzer and less power, and touchy on forehand and sidearm throws. Asher Anders preferred putting with it and throwing the Prodigy PA-3 instead, while Ben Propes, comparing the thin, shallow profile with the Prodigy PA-3, found the PA-5 flips like a seasoned putter and is not meant to go super far.

highlights.text: works for turnovers and tight lines
touchy on forehand and sidearm throws

paras: Reviewers praise it as a very understable fairway driver that is easy to flip up, fun for pop-up turnover shots and good as a roller. One reviewer calls it a fantastic disc for lower arm speeds, kids, women and masters players, while unsure that a roller this slow earns a place for a faster arm, and unsure it holds up on forehand. Disc Golf Skulboy found a prototype Proton Ascend held the line with more fade than the Kastaplast Stig, and found the turn close to the rated number.

highlights.text: fantastic disc for lower arm speeds
unsure that a roller this slow earns a place

paras: Reviewers praise it as a controllable, slightly understable midrange that is comfortable in the hand and goes far for a mid, with one calling it the best disc in the whole line. The main catch is that it can run flippy on forehand for two reviewers, and the Neutron was the most stable of three plastics, with the Cosmic Neutron holding straighter and the soft Proton the most understable. Swanky Disc Golf said it competes with the Axiom Hex, Discmania Origin and Discmania MD1, and Garry Patton said it flies like a beaten in MVP Matrix and feels similar to the Axiom Hex in the hand.

Reviewers praise it as a very overstable but controllable fairway driver that fills the gap between overstable midranges and nine-speed drivers, with a flat top that feels comfortable on forehand and backhand. Glide is a pleasant surprise, as two reviewers rate it above the listed 2, though some hands may find the shallow, unconventional feel too weird. Six Sided Discs found it swings further left, fades harder and flies a little shorter than the Discmania FD1, and No Hassle Disc Golf found it landed within about 5 to 10 feet of the Discmania FD3 and Axiom Fireball.

Reviewers praise it as a point-and-shoot throwing putter that holds whatever angle it is given, floats to the basket and feels good in power or fan grips. Stability is where takes split: one reviewer found Aura maybe the truest run and possibly slightly understable, another found the Ethos not so soft plastic the most stable Praxis thrown, and a third noticed no flight difference between plastics. Distance reports run from about 225 ft with a touch of anhyzer to about 290 to 295 ft on one long hole, and one reviewer found the soft runs feel gummy.

highlights.text: holds whatever angle it is given

paras: Reviewers praise it as a straight, controllable throwing putter that holds the line it is thrown on and flips up from a hyzer. Takes split on feel and putting: several found the plastic gummy or slick and one found the shape awkward, and one felt it did not suit putting, while another called it a pretty incredible throwing and putting putter. Plastic and weight shift stability a little, with heavier copies straight to slightly overstable and lighter ones turning more. Cheating Lefty Disc Golf matched it with the Axiom Proxy and the Discraft Challenger SS, which is slightly more overstable, and Brook Arnold compared the torque handling to the Trash Panda Dune.

highlights.text: holds the line it is thrown on

paras: Reviewers praise the thin, fast-absorbing texture and how gently it sits on sensitive, redness-prone and acne-prone skin, with reviewers reporting no irritation, one even alongside retinoids. Results split: some saw calmer cheeks and fewer pimples within weeks, while others saw no change in redness or only mild, slow fading of marks, and a few found it a little drying or tacky. Dr. Danny Guo compares it with Paula's Choice 10% Azelaic Acid Booster, which adds salicylic acid for acne, and The Ordinary Azelaic Acid Suspension 10%, which some find grainy, while UPTgift keeps Paula's Choice 10% Azelaic Acid Booster for heavy, inflamed breakouts and uses this serum for daily redness control.

Reviewers like the water-like, quick-absorbing texture and how gentle it is, including on sensitized skin using tretinoin and on very reactive skin, and several apply it by hand or on a cotton pad. Takes split on the benefit: some saw calmer redness and quick-clearing spots, while others noticed only a light soothing feel and little else, with no glow and no change in pores. Nadia Vega finds Torriden DIVE-IN Toner more hydrating but this one more soothing.

Reviewers praise the thin, fast-absorbing texture and the calm, hydrated skin it leaves, with no irritation on dry, sensitive, oily and acne-prone skin alike. Takes split on strength: some call the hydration intense and glowy, while others found it just okay, thinner than expected, or too light for dry, flaky patches, and one disliked the nutty scent. Dr. Sarah Sheu counts it among their favorites from a big range of Anua products and ranks it above Anua Heartleaf 77 Soothing Toner, which they call bland but a solid first moisturizer step.

highlights.text: too light for dry, flaky patches

paras: Reviewers agree it is very gentle and non-stripping, a fit for dry, irritated, rosacea-prone or sensitive skin and for a light morning wash. They also agree it has no lather and will not remove makeup or sunscreen, so it works as a second cleanse, and some said it left a film or residue. Things Bloggers Lied About says it has easily surpassed CeraVe Hydrating Facial Cleanser as the go-to, while Dr Dray and Sincerely Miss Ash both prefer Aveeno Calm + Restore Oat Gel Moisturizer from the same line.

highlights.text: will not remove makeup or sunscreen

paras: Reviewers like the light, cooling gel that absorbs fast and calms redness and irritation, on sensitive, rosacea-prone, combination and oily skin alike. Takes split on moisture: some found it hydrating enough, while some said very dry skin needs a hyaluronic acid serum underneath and others found it not hydrating enough overnight, in winter or under makeup. Rudi Berry prefers it to Neutrogena Hydro Boost Gel-Cream Extra-Dry in winter for irritation or dryness but keeps that gel cream for summer, while My Skincare Regime names KraveBeauty Oat So Simple Water Cream as a similar option for irritated skin.

highlights.text: needs a hyaluronic acid serum underneath

paras: Reviewers praise it as a rich barrier cream for dry, sensitive, eczema-prone or irritated skin, from post-peel and retinoid dryness to cracked hands, and several report redness calming fast. Takes split on texture: some find it thick, greasy and slow to sink in, with a white cast until rubbed in, while others find it absorbs within minutes, and a few say it is too heavy for oily skin, though acne-prone reviewers report no clogged pores. Dr. Jenny Liu points to Avène Tolerance Control Soothing Skin Recovery Cream for rosacea flares or for anyone who dislikes the thick, pasty feel of this cream, while Dr Dray finds this one much like a similar thick barrier balm but wetter and slightly greasier.

highlights.text: thick, greasy and slow to sink in

paras: Reviewers like the cooling, soothing feel and the short ingredient list of spring water and nitrogen, using it after a shower, over makeup, before hyaluronic acid serums or to cool down in heat. Takes split on how much it does: loved-it reviewers use it for redness, itching and makeup, while one reviewer adds moisturizer right after because it cannot keep dry skin hydrated, and another rates its effect on irritated facial skin as mild to moderate and finds the nozzle hit or miss.

Reviewers like it as a gentle, low-effort cleanser for dry, normal, irritated or post-procedure skin, used in the morning, as the first step of a double cleanse or when washing the face feels like too much. Takes split on cleaning power: one reviewer says it cleanses without stripping and leaves skin soft, while another admits not loving lotion cleansers because the face feels not cleaned at all and prefers a foam. One reviewer adds that rinsing it off is better day to day than wiping alone.

Reviewers like the silky, fast-absorbing gel and its easy layering, with little irritation and a subtle glow. Takes split on results: some saw redness calm and newer or post-acne marks fade slowly, while others saw no change in stubborn, older or sun-damaged dark spots, and one found it did not deeply moisturize. Keyshana Dupuy found a rival 4% niacinamide serum worked faster and repurchased only that one, while All That She Is finds The Ordinary Niacinamide 10% + Zinc 1% worked faster than this serum, which gives extra glow and hydration.

highlights.text: stubborn, older or sun-damaged dark spots

paras: Reviewers like the watery, easy-to-rinse gel and its gentleness, with a short contact time and a glow after use, including on sensitive or atopic skin. Takes split on strength: one reviewer saw texture improve with every use, while another found it just okay, not mind-blowing, and disliked the pump, which gives tiny squirts, and a chemical smell. One reviewer adds that it can leave skin a little dry, so very dry skin may not suit it.

Reviewers praise a light, gentle gel that rinses clean and takes off sunscreen and most makeup without drying skin out. Takes split on who it suits: one reviewer recommends it for sensitive skin and thinks it fits acne-prone skin most, while another says dry, sensitive or acne-prone skin should avoid it because of the geranium maculatum oil. It adds no hydration, so a moisturizer is still needed. DEWILDESALHAB prefers a foam cleanser from the same line, which leaves them feeling less oily for the rest of the day.

highlights.text: takes off sunscreen and most makeup

paras: Reviewers praise a light gel that sinks in quickly, hydrates well and feels cooling from the metal applicator, with several noting less puffiness. Takes split on the applicator and on moisture: one says it warms up and does not always roll smoothly, another finds the roller sharp in one direction, and one calls it not very moisturizing for very dry under eyes. Banya Biswas uses it in the morning only, since the copper tripeptide does not mix well with their retinol and acid nights, and prefers Beauty of Joseon Revive Eye Serum: Ginseng + Retinal at night.

Reviewers who like it describe a hydrating, fragrance-free cream that melts in, leaves skin plump and works as a night cream or a base under sunscreen. Takes split on finish and skin type: one finds it stays sticky and pills under sunscreen or makeup, another wears it under a hydrating sunscreen without it feeling heavy, and oily skin may find it too heavy. Some broke out, and some suspect coconut oil. Simone S layers Beauty of Joseon Red Bean Water Gel over it and says the gel became their favorite of the two, and An Indian Potpourri also prefers the gel for absorbing fully with no sticky residue.

Reviewers like the very light oil texture, which turns milky or emulsifies, rinses without residue and takes off sunscreen and most makeup. Takes split on the smell, which different reviewers describe as strongly herbal, like cooking oil, like peanuts or a strong ginseng scent, and one says it is why they will not buy it again. Opinions also split on skin type: one finds it great for dry and sensitive skin but not friendly for acne-prone skin, while another saw little bumps and stopped using it. My Skincare Regime finds the texture similar to SKIN1004 Centella Light Cleansing Oil, though they describe that one as scented.

Reviewers praise a very light, water-like ginseng toner that sinks in fast, soothes sensitive and reactive skin and works as a toner, essence or both. Takes split on hydration: some call it very hydrating, even for oily and combination skin, while others find it only moderately hydrating, and one with oily combination skin found it left skin dry and tight. Archee Gupta finds it slightly thicker and smoother than Beauty of Joseon Green Plum Refreshing Toner: AHA + BHA and rates it above Beauty of Joseon Glow Replenishing Rice Milk, which they found not hydrating enough in extreme winter.

Reviewers praise a watery, scent-free serum that absorbs quickly, leaves a slight glow and is gentle on most skin. Takes split on results: some saw dark spots, acne scars or uneven tone fade over weeks, while others saw little or no change in brightness after months, and one very sensitive reviewer developed reddish spots and stopped after three uses. For hyperpigmentation on the cheeks, alex greyson finds the feel almost identical to Beauty of Joseon Glow Serum: Propolis + Niacinamide and the fading faster, though the other serum did more for texture and acne. Nayatilly finds it far less effective than a ginseng and snail mucin serum from the same line, and says The INKEY List Hyaluronic Acid Serum adds moisture much better.

highlights.text: absorbs quickly, leaves a slight glow
little or no change in brightness

paras: Reviewers describe a very watery toner that sinks in quickly, adds light hydration and a soft glow, and is usually patted on by hand. Takes split on who it suits: oily and combination skin tends to like it, one says it is best suited to dry skin, and others say dry or mature skin needs more layers or a cream. A Woman's Confidence is less excited by it than by richer, more luscious milky toners, and JQ LEEJQ, who has very dry skin, says a richer cream toner they tried since has raised their expectations. No BS Beauty scores it seven against nine for a rice toner from another brand, preferring that toner's less tacky finish.

highlights.text: sinks in quickly, adds light hydration
needs more layers or a cream

paras: Reviewers like a light serum that is slightly tacky at first, then absorbs fast, adds a dewy glow, calms redness and pimples and layers well under moisturizer and sunscreen. Takes split by skin type: very oily skin may find it too dewy or shiny under makeup, and very dry skin may want more hydration, while sensitive and acne-prone skin did well on it. Comparing textures, jessmeandering finds it similar to COSRX Advanced Snail 96 Mucin Power Essence, while Kelly Driscoll calls it the acne serum of three from the same line and prefers a calming green tea serum from that line for sensitive, dehydrated skin.

highlights.text: too dewy or shiny under makeup

paras: Reviewers like a mild gel that turns into a soft foam, rinses clean and leaves skin comfortable, with a very light fruity or fresh scent. Takes split on dryness: some found it stripping, leaving skin squeaky clean or drying in winter, while others found it soft and not tight, with no irritation on sensitive or breakout-prone skin. It removes sunscreen and light makeup easily, but heavy or waterproof makeup, mascara and eyeliner need a separate remover or a second cleanse. Doctor Anne uses it as a second cleanse after Beauty of Joseon Radiance Cleansing Balm, while Miss LJ Beauty says the cleansers they usually go back to last longer than this one.

highlights.text: rinses clean and leaves skin comfortable

paras: Reviewers who like it describe a very watery toner with gentle AHA and BHA that they say helps with texture and pores on sensitive or reactive skin without sensitivity. Both advise easing in, no more than three nights a week for one and about every other night for the other, and one notes it adds no hydration. Dr. Vanita Rattan would not recommend it to skin of colour, since the glycolic acid used morning and night risks irritation, though they like pairing an AHA with a BHA. Archee Gupta finds Beauty of Joseon Ginseng Essence Water slightly thicker and better for irritated skin, and calls Beauty of Joseon Glow Replenishing Rice Milk a miss.

Reviewers mostly praise this rice and honey wash-off mask for leaving skin soft, bright and calm without the tightness of many clay masks, with several saying redness settled after the first use. Takes split on skin type and smell: some call it right for dry skin, others say it suits oily or acne-prone skin better, and the rice scent is called unpleasant by several. Manisha Mishra alternates it with Beauty of Joseon Red Bean Refreshing Pore Mask, which they pick for oilier skin, and Kelly Driscoll prefers it to Beauty of Joseon Glow Replenishing Rice Milk, whose clay left their skin tight. alex greyson found it the least drying kaolin mask they have tried but dislikes physical exfoliators and is unsure about buying it again.

Reviewers like this stick for midday reapplication: it glides on, dries matte or satin and feels light, with no white cast and no clogged pores reported. Takes split on whether it can do more than top up: one reviewer was mixed because the stick format needs many swipes, misses spots and is not water or sweat proof, and another also needs at least four passes per area. Sarah Rose ranks it third of nine sticks, finding one rival stick more weightless and another more hydrating. One reviewer warns it may be too drying for dry skin.

highlights.text: no white cast and no clogged pores

paras: Reviewers like this red bean clay mask for staying comfortable, not drying or hardening, and for slightly smoother pores, even on dry skin. Takes split on strength: one reviewer calls it a decent mild exfoliant for oilier skin but notes a strong scent and scratchy seeds, and two say it does not clear blackheads. Manisha Mishra calls Beauty of Joseon Ground Rice and Honey Glow Mask the better pick for dull, dry or sensitive skin, since it hydrates more, and suggests alternating the two.

Reviewers like this gel for its cooling, fast-absorbing, non-sticky feel, with no breakouts or clogged pores reported and a fragrance-free formula. Most pick it for oily, combination or acne-prone skin, while those with dry skin add a richer cream on top or layer it over a serum, and results are described as moisture and feel rather than dramatic change. Michelle Bali points dry skin to Beauty of Joseon Dynasty Cream instead, while An Indian Potpourri prefers this gel to that cream, finding the cream a little sticky at first and linking it to their acne. Kelly Driscoll picks it over a thinner oat gel cream whose hydration did not last on their skin.

highlights.text: add a richer cream on top

paras: Reviewers mostly praise the weightless, water-like feel and the lack of white cast, saying it sits well under makeup and suits oily or combination skin better than dry skin. Not everyone agrees: one reviewer got stinging and an itchy body rash they suspect comes from a salicylate booster, and another found it tacky, heavy and shiny in humid weather. Who What Wear and Kelly Driscoll compare it with Beauty of Joseon Relief Sun: Rice + Probiotics SPF 50+, finding this one lighter and the original creamier, with the original better for dry skin or winter. clarity kat found it the lightest of four sunscreens they tried but named Haruharu Wonder Black Rice Moisture Airyfit Daily Sunscreen the overall winner.

highlights.text: stinging and an itchy body rash
tacky, heavy and shiny in humid weather

paras: Reviewers praise the light, cream-like texture that melts in without pilling, with a soft glow, no real white cast and little scent, and several say it works under makeup. Takes split on the eyes and on shine: some report no stinging even on delicate eyes, while others get stinging if it reaches them, and very oily skin may find it too glowy. Protection is debated: one reviewer saw a slight tan after about an hour in harsh sun, and another found foundation over it reduced the layer on a UV camera. Paulina Esquivel prefers it to Beauty of Joseon Relief Sun Aqua-Fresh: Rice + B5 SPF 50+, which controls shine a little better but looks less luminous and can pill.

Reviewers like this light, quick-absorbing retinal serum for being gentle around sensitive eyes while slowly softening fine lines and brightening the under-eye area. Takes split on results and feel: most call it a gradual, gentle option, one noted it does not fix dark circles caused by poor sleep, and another found the texture slightly oily and heavier. Reviewers also advise night use, sunscreen by day, starting a couple of times a week and keeping it off the eyelid margin.

highlights.text: dark circles caused by poor sleep

paras: Reviewers praise how gently this micellar water cleans, with no perfume, no stinging around the eyes and no oily film, including on sensitive, rosacea-prone and dry skin. Takes split on makeup removal: one reviewer clears eye makeup in a single swipe and another lifts waterproof makeup with gentle pats, while another says waterproof mascara is the one thing it will not lift and heavy makeup takes several passes. The mixed reviewer got burning and redness after applying it with a baby wipe, which they blame on ignoring the label's cotton pad directions.

Reviewers praise the thin, silky milky texture that absorbs fast, leaves a glow without residue and stays gentle on sensitive and reddened skin. Takes split on weight and need: some call it light enough for oily skin and hydrating enough for dry skin, while others find it hydrating but barely moisturizing and not a must-have. Dr Dray prefers a creamier toner with macadamia seed oil after a couple of weeks and would not repurchase this one, and Made-up Mesearch ranks it a close second to Haruharu Wonder Black Rice Hyaluronic Toner.

highlights.text: thin, silky milky texture that absorbs fast

paras: Reviewers like this creamy 4% benzoyl peroxide wash for being easy to tolerate, with ceramides, hyaluronic acid and niacinamide in the base, and for cleaning without much dryness, though several note it foams little. Takes split on results: some saw blemishes clear or mask-related breakouts drop, while one found it did not help moderate hormonal acne and one very oily reviewer disliked the film it leaves. Dr Dray finds it more moisturizing and easier to tolerate on the face than another brand's 4% benzoyl peroxide creamy wash, though too slippery to work as a shower body mask.

highlights.text: did not help moderate hormonal acne

paras: Reviewers praise it as a two-in-one SPF 30 moisturizer that does not feel oily and, for several of them, caused no breakouts on acne-prone or sensitive skin. Takes split on texture: some saw no white cast at all, while others saw a white tint or coating at first that took time and rubbing to blend. Niella Obijiaku found it thicker and whiter than CeraVe PM Facial Moisturizing Lotion, which they rate as the lighter, clearer option. Allura Beauty saw it pill when layered over another moisturizer and chose a drugstore SPF 30 lotion with near-identical ingredients instead.

highlights.text: a white tint or coating at first
pill when layered over another moisturizer

paras: Reviewers mostly praise how light and quick to absorb it is, using it on the body and face with no sticky feel, and often pick it for normal, combination, oily or sweaty skin. Takes split on dryness: Mis Fashionerias On-line found CeraVe Moisturizing Cream thicker and better for dry to extra dry skin, while Olivia UKBeautyRoom, whose skin is extremely dry, finds the lotion a bit more moisturizing than CeraVe Moisturizing Cream and suggests the cream for winter. Cotton Candy Fro found it not moisturizing enough for drier patches and broke out after one use on a combination oily face, and No BS Beauty warns acne-prone skin off the face.

highlights.text: not moisturizing enough for drier patches
warns acne-prone skin off the face

paras: Reviewers mostly like it as a gentle, lightweight eye cream that hydrates and sits smoothly under concealer, with no stinging even on sensitive eyes. Results are where takes split: some saw slightly calmer puffiness and dark circles, while others saw no help for dark circles. Matt Randon compared the ingredient list with CeraVe PM Facial Moisturizing Lotion and found the same key ingredients, with the eye cream only slightly thicker, so two layers of the lotion would do the same job. Olivia UKBeautyRoom found it a bit thinner than they prefer and would pick a much richer eye cream.

Reviewers mostly praise it as a gentle, fragrance-free cleanser that foams and lifts oil, dirt and makeup without leaving skin dry or tight, especially on oily, combination and acne-prone skin. Takes split on dryness: one reviewer was left with tight, not-soft skin, while others felt no tightness at all and some saw fewer pimples. Dr. Daniel Sugai picks it over CeraVe Hydrating Facial Cleanser for acne-prone skin because it has niacinamide, and Oluchi Onuigbo points normal to dry skin to CeraVe Hydrating Facial Cleanser instead. Dr. Arsalan Aspires suggests sensitive skin wanting fewer actives may lean toward a simpler foaming cleanser with a self-foaming pump.

highlights.text: without leaving skin dry or tight

paras: Reviewers praise it as a night-time slugging step that seals in moisture and calms dry, flaky or retinol-irritated skin, with the ceramides and hyaluronic acid as the reason it feels better than plain petroleum jelly. Dr Dray found it plumper and better on fine lines around the eyes and on lips than a competing petrolatum ointment that contains lanolin, though that one stays the pick for first aid, while All That Glows calls it a step above plain petroleum jelly and James Welsh slightly prefers it to plain petroleum jelly. Takes split on feel and skin type: it can stay greasy and sticky for hours, may leave product on the pillow, and some reviewers hold back from recommending it for acne-prone skin, though one with acne-prone skin says it never broke them out.

highlights.text: a step above plain petroleum jelly

paras: Reviewers who loved it describe a creamy cleanser that foams a little, rinses clean and removes makeup and sunscreen without leaving skin tight or dry, including on dry, sensitive and acne-prone skin. Takes split on makeup removal and irritation: some needed two or three washes or an oil first for mascara and waxy products, and one reviewer got pimples and a chin reaction within days. Lavinia Rusanda calls it the best of both worlds between CeraVe Hydrating Facial Cleanser and CeraVe Foaming Facial Cleanser, while Oluchi Onuigbo finds it less drying than the foaming one and liked it more than the hydrating one, which did not work for them. Twenty4kay prefers it to CeraVe Hydrating Facial Cleanser for more moisture and better makeup removal.

Reviewers mostly like it as a soft, non-stripping cleanser with no scent and little or no lather, best for normal to dry, sensitive or winter-flaky skin. Takes split on oily skin and makeup: some found a film left behind and said it does not lift mascara, sebum or full makeup in one wash. DSBOSSKO found slightly more hydration and barrier repair than Cetaphil Gentle Skin Cleanser but picked no clear winner, and Saloni Alok Jain found their skin felt softer than with Cetaphil Gentle Skin Cleanser. Oluchi Onuigbo and Matt Randon both reach for CeraVe Foaming Facial Cleanser when skin runs oilier.

Reviewers praise it as a rich, thick seal for dry, flaky or eczema-prone skin that works on face, hands and body without fragrance. Takes split on weight and finish: some found it absorbs quickly and sits well under makeup, others found it slow to sink in, sticky or pilling, and several say it is too heavy for oily or acne-prone faces. Chitranshi preferred CeraVe Daily Moisturizing Lotion for its faster absorption, while Jime Mitzunaga preferred this cream to CeraVe Daily Moisturizing Lotion because it uses less product and absorbs faster.

highlights.text: too heavy for oily or acne-prone faces

paras: Reviewers mostly like it as a very light, quick-absorbing lotion with no residue that works at night, under makeup or in the morning with a separate sunscreen. Takes split on skin type: some found it hydrating all night on combination or dry skin, while others found it not moisturizing enough for cheeks, neck or dry areas, and sensitive skin reported tingling or burning. Beautiful With Brains is not a huge fan of CeraVe AM Facial Moisturizing Lotion with Sunscreen, which they find lightweight but not very hydrating, while Pure Glam Guide prefers this PM version over that one, which can feel thicker and leave a white cast. Zuko Nyaawie picks it over CeraVe Daily Moisturizing Lotion for its silky texture, and skyforce95 Reviews found CeraVe Moisturizing Cream too heavy and suffocating next to this lotion.

Reviewers mostly like it as an everyday gel cleanser that lathers well, cleans without a scrubby feel and adds gentle salicylic acid exfoliation for blackheads, bumps and breakouts on oily, combination or acne-prone skin. Takes split on sensitivity: several found it fine even on dry, sensitive skin, while others felt tingling, a sting around the nose or eyes, or irritation the next day, and some saw no improvement. Dr. Janet calls it CeraVe Foaming Facial Cleanser with extra exfoliating ingredients and swaps between the two, while Soso Models found it gentler than CeraVe Acne Foaming Cream Cleanser, which dried their skin out.

Reviewers praise a lightweight, gel-like serum that absorbs quickly and is gentle enough for a first retinol, with dark spots and post-acne marks fading for some reviewers over about a month. One reviewer who used it nightly for eight weeks saw no change in dark spots and noticed forehead zits, and another found two weeks too short to judge retinol results. Dr. Arsalan Aspires sets this blue bottle against a richer, creamier retinol serum in a purple bottle from the same brand, which suits dry and mature skin better, and calls this one the pick for post-acne marks and textured skin.

highlights.text: gentle enough for a first retinol
saw no change in dark spots

paras: Reviewers praise a very thick cream that leaves skin soft and plump by morning, with little to no scent and a velvety finish. Takes split on oily and acne-prone skin: one reviewer with oily skin used it nightly and loved it, while another found their face started to freak out after a few nights, especially around the nose, and kept it for the neck and dry patches. Others note that very oily skin should build up slowly or skip it.

highlights.text: freak out after a few nights

paras: Reviewers mostly praise a thin, hydrating serum that absorbs fast and layers well under sunscreen and makeup, with 10% L-ascorbic acid that feels easier on skin than stronger versions and caused little or no stinging for most. Takes split on staying power: several reviewers found the serum oxidizes quickly, turning orange or brown, and a few had tubes that leaked, cracked or came with loose caps. Sensitive skin is the other split, as one reviewer with acne-prone skin broke out repeatedly and another flagged the denatured alcohol as possibly drying, while others with sensitive or dry skin saw no irritation.

highlights.text: absorbs fast and layers well under sunscreen
oxidizes quickly, turning orange or brown

paras: Reviewers praise a silky, lightweight lotion that absorbs fast, leaves no white cast and sits well under makeup, with oily, combination and sensitive skin the best fits. Takes split on moisture and finish: one reviewer found it too matte and not moisturizing enough for dry, dehydrated skin, while others call the finish natural or glowy rather than truly matte. Dr. Daniel Sugai prefers it to the thicker CeraVe AM Facial Moisturizing Lotion with Sunscreen in summer, noting the AM lotion adds niacinamide for acne-prone skin, and benenon says the AM lotion pilled and balled up on their bare skin.

highlights.text: absorbs fast, leaves no white cast
not moisturizing enough for dry, dehydrated skin

paras: Reviewers praise a soapless, low-foam lotion that cleans without tightness and is gentle enough for sensitive, dry or reactive skin, and even works without water. The split is oily and acne-prone skin: one reviewer found it did not cleanse as much on oily skin in humid heat, and another would not recommend it for acne-prone or oily skin. Dr.Chiyen compares it with Cetaphil Daily Facial Cleanser and other versions, calling this one the choice with the fewest ingredients and lowest irritation risk.

highlights.text: not cleanse as much on oily skin

paras: Reviewers like a light gel-cream that absorbs quickly, feels comfortable around the eyes and layers under concealer without sliding. They saw little change in eye bags, dark circles or fine lines, and those with drier eyes wanted something richer. Dr. Aleksandra Brown DO, FAAD picks it for daytime and makeup, and CeraVe Eye Repair Cream for night on very dry, crepey under-eyes, while No BS Beauty prefers COSRX Advanced Snail Peptide Eye Cream for day because sunscreen does not set well over this one.

Reviewers praise a thick, rich cream that absorbs well without a greasy residue and leaves skin hydrated, with sensitive and acne-prone skin reporting no irritation or new breakouts. One reviewer loves it in winter but says it may not be best for oily skin in summer, and another saw eczema and allergy patches keep coming back, although it soothed the itching. The Pink Velvet Blog finds it thicker and more intense than a slightly runnier daily hydrating lotion from the same brand, and says it works on the face as well as the body.

highlights.text: absorbs well without a greasy residue

paras: Reviewers who liked the patches used them overnight on whiteheads and pimples that already had a head, and saw smaller, less red spots by morning, with several noting they stop picking. Takes split on closed and cystic spots and on looks: some reviewers saw no change on deep or hidden pimples, a few found the patches visible in daylight or peeling with sweat, and others call them nearly invisible. Brianna Jane prefers Mario Badescu Drying Lotion for speed, saying it worked better for them, though the patches stayed on all night where a lotion does not.

highlights.text: smaller, less red spots by morning
no change on deep or hidden pimples

paras: Reviewers praise a lightweight-feeling gel-cream that hydrates, soothes irritated or over-exfoliated skin and leaves a dewy, glassy glow, mostly on oily, combination or sensitive skin. Takes split on dryness and breakouts: one reviewer with very dry, eczema-prone skin found it stinging and drying, others with dry skin layer a thicker cream on top, and a few with oily or acne-prone skin saw breakouts. The texture is the other split, with reviewers calling it slimy, stringy or tacky and slow to sink in. Kelly Driscoll calls it a thicker gel cream with the same hydrating feel as COSRX Advanced Snail 96 Mucin Power Essence, while JQ LEEJQ likens the jelly texture to Beauty of Joseon Dynasty Cream, which they love.

highlights.text: layer a thicker cream on top

paras: Reviewers praise the hydration most: skin looks plump, soft and glassy straight after applying, and it absorbs quickly with no reaction on sensitive, combination or acne-prone skin. Takes split on what else it does: some saw calmer post-pimple redness or a softer barrier, others saw no change in acne marks or texture, and some say it supports hydration rather than transforming skin. The sticky, slimy feel can be more noticeable on oily skin, and Dr Dray cannot say whether it differs from a plain hyaluronic acid serum, since the formula already contains sodium hyaluronate, and notes the humectants need a moisturizer on top.

highlights.text: no change in acne marks or texture

paras: Reviewers mostly praise a lightweight, fast-absorbing cream that hydrates the eye area without stinging and sits well under makeup, which they say suits sensitive or easily irritated eyes. Takes split on results: some saw slightly less puffiness or a mild lift, while others saw no change in dark circles or fine lines, and peptide effects are said to need months. Dr. Ashwini Megur found COSRX Advanced Snail 96 Mucin Power Essence gave the same results and was the better pick for them, while Kelly Driscoll reads this cream as a step up from COSRX Advanced Snail 92 All in One Cream for the eye area.

Reviewers who loved it use it once a week or a few nights a week for smoother texture and small bumps on the chin and forehead, and Becca M sets it beside Sunday Riley Good Genes Lactic Acid Treatment, calling this one the plainer option with more product. Takes split on whiteheads: some saw small bumps clear, while others saw no change after weeks or months. Irritation splits too, from no stinging for some to redness and burning when used too often or in large amounts, so reviewers kept use to a few times a week at most.

highlights.text: saw no change after weeks or months
redness and burning when used too often

paras: Reviewers who loved it praise a gentle, watery toner used several times a week or nightly, with smaller-looking pores, fewer visible blackheads and no stinging, and many like the fine mist. Takes split on strength: one reviewer found it too mild to change sebaceous filaments or closed comedones, while others saw slightly clearer skin and cleaner pores. Matt Randon still prefers COSRX BHA Blackhead Power Liquid for its thicker essence feel and its help with redness, while liking this toner as AHA and BHA in one. One reviewer found it hot and irritating from the first use and pointed to a low pH.

Reviewers who loved it describe a creamy, aloe-based sunscreen that blends without white cast and hydrates enough to skip moisturizer on dry or combination skin. Takes split on skin type: oily and humid-weather users found it heavy or greasy, while others with combination oily or acne-prone skin got a skin-like finish. Pilling is the sticking point for some, as are the fragrance and alcohol in the formula, and one reviewer doubted the SPF 50+ claim until independent results are published.

Reviewers praise a rich, deeply hydrating cream that calms dry, irritated skin and retinol dryness, and they like the opaque tube as more hygienic than a jar. Takes split on daytime wear: Musings of a Muse finds it lighter and easier to wear by day than a heavier ceramide cream from another brand, while others find it too thick and hard to layer under sunscreen and makeup. Oily or acne-prone skin may find it too thick, and the bergamot oil scent bothers some even as others barely notice it.

Reviewers who liked it describe a watery, moisturizing BHA with no strong smell that does not dry the skin, used once to a few times a week, and they see it as a fit for beginners to exfoliation. Results are the split: some saw fewer blackheads and less oil within a week to a month, while others saw little change because it contains betaine salicylate rather than salicylic acid itself. Tamuno Abbey compared it side by side with Paula's Choice SKIN PERFECTING 2% BHA Liquid Exfoliant and prefers that one, which shrank pimples overnight, while this one showed nothing after half a bottle.

Reviewers who loved it praise instant, soothing hydration and a soft glow that layers well, mostly on dry, dehydrated, sensitive or acne-prone skin, with no stinging even on reactive skin. Opinion splits on oily skin and texture: one reviewer found it sticky and oily on very oily skin, and others call it slightly viscous or a little sticky when built up in layers. Banya Biswas ranks it above COSRX Advanced Snail 96 Mucin Power Essence among the COSRX toners and essences tried, and AliceintheRabbitHole ranks it first ahead of COSRX Full Fit Propolis Honey Overnight Mask.

highlights.text: sticky and oily on very oily skin

paras: Reviewers who loved it praise a gel that lathers lightly and cleans without stripping or tightness on oily, combination and sensitive skin, with the tea tree scent liked by some and called strong by others. The split is hydration and makeup: some say it is not hydrating, can dry skin in dry climates, and will not remove waterproof mascara or eye makeup. One reviewer broke out painfully on three tries, and a couple of reviewers said it stung their eyes.

Reviewers loved it as a gentle BHA step that leaves pores looking smaller and cleaner, with no stinging, dryness or irritation, and one pad covers the whole face. Takes differ on scent: one reviewer finds a strong medicinal smell, probably from tea tree and orange peel oil, while another notes a subtle citrus scent. The Happy Sloths compares it with COSRX AHA/BHA Clarifying Treatment Toner, finding that toner's very similar formula much gentler than salicylic acid but meant for glow in all skin types, while this pad adds tea tree oil and suits acne-prone skin.

Reviewers praise a creamy cleanser that makes a rich foam from a small amount and cleans oily, acne-prone skin without irritation, with less oil and fewer or smaller blemishes after a few weeks. The split is feel: one reviewer found it thick and greasy with an astringent finish and a lemony smell, while others found it soft, smooth and moisturizing. Jello Beans uses COSRX Low pH Good Morning Gel Cleanser in the morning and this one at night as the second step of a two-step cleanse.

Reviewers praise it as a thin, quick-absorbing first step that suits oily, sensitive and combination skin and layers under almost anything. Takes split on results: some saw clearer hydration and calmer skin, while others noticed no change in texture or redness, or in fine lines, and called it closer to a toner than a serum. Kelly Driscoll found fewer results than expected next to The Ordinary Multi-Peptide + HA Serum and rated it a booster, not a main anti-aging serum.

highlights.text: no change in texture or redness

paras: Reviewers praise it as a fragrance-free, ceramide-rich cream that hydrates without greasiness, works under makeup and sunscreen, and suits dry, sensitive, mature and combination skin. Takes differ on weight: some found it silky and quick to absorb, while others found it slow to settle, too light for dry skin in cold weather, or heavy by day on oily skin. The Strategist found the texture like CeraVe Moisturizing Cream but thicker, and kept it as the everyday option beside a richer, more expensive favorite.

highlights.text: heavy by day on oily skin

paras: Reviewers recommend it as an entry-level retinol cream, praising a light texture that sinks in without greasiness and little or no irritation, even over eczema flare-ups in one case. Takes split on results and value: some saw firmer, plumper skin and fading dark spots, while others saw no dramatic change and found the small tube poor value. alex greyson found it no different in feel from a cheaper gentle retinol cream and called it overpriced for the amount.

Reviewers who used it praise a silky, non-greasy oil that caused no irritation, even on sensitive areas and for people used to stronger retinoids. Views split on who it fits: one reviewer calls it well suited to dry skin new to retinol but warns the soybean oil can clog pores on oily skin, while another used it almost nightly on oily skin without trouble.
